using namespace M;
using namespace Driver;
using namespace std::string_literals;

Python::Device::Device(M::DeviceSpec deviceSpec,
                       M::Driver::DeviceContextRef ctx)
    : deviceSpec(std::move(deviceSpec)), ctx(std::move(ctx)) {}

std::string Python::Device::getAsString() const {
  std::string str;
  llvm::raw_string_ostream oss(str);
  oss << "Device(type=" << deviceSpec.ref.label << ",";
  oss << "id=" << deviceSpec.ref.id << ")";
  return str;
}

ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceBufferRef>
Python::Device::allocateBuffer(const TensorSpec &spec, bool pinned) const {
  return M::GraphCompiler::Driver::allocateDeviceBuffer(ctx, spec, pinned);
}

M::Driver::DeviceBufferRef Python::Device::allocate(const TensorSpec &spec,
                                                    bool pinned) {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceBufferRef> bufOr = allocateBuffer(spec, pinned);
  if (bufOr.isError())
    throw std::invalid_argument(bufOr.getError());
  return bufOr.takeValue();
}

M::Driver::DeviceBufferRef Python::Device::wrapExternalBuffer(
    void *data, const TensorSpec &spec,
    llvm::unique_function<void()> destructor) const {
  M::Driver::DeviceBufferRef buf =
      ctx->createBufferOwning(data, spec.getSizeInBytes(), /*owning=*/true);
  buf->setDestructorFn(std::move(destructor));
  return buf;
}

std::string Python::Device::getLabel() const { return deviceSpec.ref.label; }

uint64_t Python::Device::getId() const { return deviceSpec.ref.id; }

bool Python::Device::isHost() const {
  return ctx->device().api() == M::Driver::Device::cpuAPI;
}

M::AsyncRT::CPUDeviceRef Python::CPU::getAsyncRTCPUDevice() const {
  // `Python::CPU` is only constructed by `getCpuDevice`, which creates the
  // context against `Device::cpuAPI`, so it is always a `CpuDeviceContext`.
  // The downcast helper asserts this contract.
#if MODULAR_HAL_DEVICE_CONTEXT
  // The HAL DeviceContext has no CpuDeviceContext subclass to reach through.
  // Use the same process-wide AsyncRT CPUDevice that CpuDeviceContext creates
  // (same source and options), so all consumers share one CPUDevice.
  M::AsyncRT::CPUDeviceRef cpuDevice = M::AsyncRT::getOrCreateCPUDevice(
      M::AsyncRT::CPUDeviceSource::CPUDeviceContext,
      M::AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions().withMainWillNotDonate(),
      /*allowUsingExistingOptions=*/true);
#else
  const M::Driver::CpuDeviceContext &cpuCtx =
      M::Driver::CpuDeviceContext::cast(*ctx);
  M::AsyncRT::CPUDeviceRef cpuDevice = cpuCtx.getCPUDevice();
#endif
  if (!cpuDevice) {
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "max.driver.CPU has no associated AsyncRT CPUDevice");
  }
  return cpuDevice;
}

std::unique_ptr<Python::Detail::AsyncHostFuncUserData>
Python::CPU::makeAsyncHostFuncUserData(nb::object fn,
                                       const CompletionFlag &flag,
                                       std::uint64_t value) const {
  // `flag.ref().copy()` bumps the RCRef; the AsyncRT worker holds it
  // for the duration of the task so the MLRT allocation outlives the
  // Python wrapper's GC state.
  return std::make_unique<Detail::AsyncHostFuncUserData>(
      Detail::AsyncHostFuncUserData{
          /*task=*/{std::move(fn), flag.ref().copy(), value},
          /*cpuDeviceRef=*/getAsyncRTCPUDevice(),
      });
}

std::string Python::Device::getStats() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<M::Driver::Device::MemInfo> infoOr = ctx->getMemoryInfo();
  if (infoOr.isError()) {
    std::string errorMessage =
        "failed to get device stats: "s + infoOr.getError();
    throw std::runtime_error(errorMessage);
  }
  M::Driver::Device::MemInfo info = infoOr.get();

  std::string s;
  llvm::raw_string_ostream os(s);
  llvm::json::OStream j(os);

  j.object([&] {
    j.attribute("free_memory", info.free);
    j.attribute("total_memory", info.total);
    ErrorOr<M::Driver::Device::GraphMemInfo> graphMemResult =
        ctx->device().getGraphMemoryInfo();
    if (!graphMemResult.isError()) {
      M::Driver::Device::GraphMemInfo graphMem = graphMemResult.takeValue();
      j.attribute("graph_mem_reserved", graphMem.reserved);
      j.attribute("graph_mem_used", graphMem.used);
    }
  });

  os.flush();
  return s;
}

size_t Python::Device::getMaxSingleAllocSize() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<size_t> sizeOr = ctx->device().maxSingleAllocationSize();
  if (sizeOr.isError()) {
    std::string errorMessage =
        "failed to get device max single allocation size: "s +
        sizeOr.getError();
    throw std::runtime_error(errorMessage);
  }
  return sizeOr.get();
}

std::pair<uintptr_t, size_t>
Python::Device::getAllocationRange(uintptr_t address) const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<M::Driver::Device::AllocationRange> rangeOr =
      ctx->device().allocationRange(reinterpret_cast<void *>(address));
  if (rangeOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error("failed to get the allocation range: "s +
                             rangeOr.getError());
  return {reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(rangeOr->base), rangeOr->size};
}

bool Python::Device::isHostUnified() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<bool> unifiedOr = ctx->device().isHostUnified();
  if (unifiedOr.isError()) {
    std::string errorMessage =
        "failed to query whether device memory is unified with the host: "s +
        unifiedOr.getError();
    throw std::runtime_error(errorMessage);
  }
  return unifiedOr.get();
}

std::string Python::Device::getApi() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  return ctx->device().api().str();
}

std::string Python::Device::getArchName() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<const char *> archNameOr = ctx->device().getArchName();
  if (archNameOr.isError()) {
    std::string errorMessage =
        "failed to get device architecture name: "s + archNameOr.getError();
    throw std::invalid_argument(errorMessage);
  }
  return archNameOr.get();
}

std::string Python::Device::getModelName() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  return ctx->device().name();
}

Python::PyDeviceStreamTy Python::Device::defaultStream() {
  return std::make_unique<Python::DeviceStream>(*this, this->ctx);
}

bool Python::Device::isCompatible() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOrSuccess compatibleOr = ctx->device().isCompatible();
  if (compatibleOr.isError()) {
    throw std::runtime_error(compatibleOr.getError());
  }
  return true;
}

void Python::Device::synchronize() const {
  // Release the GIL so host callbacks enqueued via `enqueue_host_func`
  // (which need to acquire the GIL to invoke Python) can make progress
  // while we wait for the device to drain.
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  if (auto errOr = ctx->synchronize(); errOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(errOr.getError());
}

bool Python::Device::canAccess(const Device &other) const {
  ErrorOr<bool> canAccessOr = ctx->device().canAccess(other.ctx->device());
  if (canAccessOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(canAccessOr.getError());
  return *canAccessOr;
}

bool Python::Device::operator==(const Device &other) const {
  return this->deviceSpec.ref == other.deviceSpec.ref;
}

bool Python::Device::operator!=(const Device &other) const {
  return !(*this == other);
}

Python::DeviceEvent::DeviceEvent(M::Driver::DeviceEventRef ev) : ev(ev) {}

Python::DeviceEvent::DeviceEvent(Device &device, bool enable_timing)
    : ev(createEventFromDevice(device, enable_timing)) {}

M::Driver::DeviceEventRef
Python::DeviceEvent::createEventFromDevice(Device &device, bool enable_timing) {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceEventRef> eventOr =
      device.ctx->eventCreate(enable_timing);
  if (eventOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(eventOr.getError());
  return *eventOr;
}

std::string Python::DeviceEvent::getAsString() const {
  std::stringstream ss;
  ss << ev->device().api().str() << "[" << ev->device().id() << "]:event@"
     << static_cast<const void *>(ev.getPointer());
  return ss.str();
}

void Python::DeviceEvent::synchronize() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOrSuccess err = ev->synchronize();
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());
}

bool Python::DeviceEvent::isReady() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<bool> err = ev->isReady();
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());
  return *err;
}

float Python::DeviceEvent::elapsedTime(const DeviceEvent &end) const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<float> millis = ev->elapsedTime(*end.ev);
  if (millis.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(millis.getError());
  return *millis;
}

bool Python::DeviceEvent::operator==(const DeviceEvent &other) const {
  // Events are equal if they refer to the same underlying event object
  return ev.getPointer() == other.ev.getPointer();
}

Python::DeviceStream::DeviceStream(Python::PyDeviceTy device)
    : dev(device), stream(std::move(device)) {}

Python::DeviceStream::DeviceStream(Device &device,
                                   M::Driver::DeviceContextRef context)
    : dev(device.shared_from_this()),
      stream(std::make_shared<Device>(dev->deviceSpec, std::move(context))) {}

Python::DeviceStream::~DeviceStream() {}

std::string Python::DeviceStream::getAsString() const {
  void *streamPtr = nullptr;
  if (*(stream->ctx) != *(dev->ctx)) {
    auto err = stream->ctx->stream();
    if (!err.isError())
      streamPtr = (*err)->ptr();
  }
  std::stringstream ss;
  if (streamPtr == nullptr) {
    ss << stream->ctx->device().api().str() << "[" << stream->ctx->device().id()
       << "]";
  } else {
    ss << stream->ctx->device().api().str() << "[" << stream->ctx->device().id()
       << ", " << streamPtr << "]";
  }
  return ss.str();
}

void Python::DeviceStream::synchronize() const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOrSuccess err = stream->ctx->synchronize();
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());
}

void Python::DeviceStream::waitFor(const DeviceStream &stream) const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOrSuccess err = this->stream->ctx->enqueueWaitFor(*stream.stream->ctx);
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());
}

Python::PyDeviceEventTy Python::DeviceStream::enqueueEvent() {

      *(this->stream->ctx->enqueueEvent()));

void Python::DeviceStream::enqueueEvent(const DeviceEvent &event) const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOrSuccess err = this->stream->ctx->enqueueEvent(*event.ev);
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());
}

namespace {

// Owns the Python callable whose refcount must be managed under the GIL.
struct HostFuncUserData {
  nb::object fn;
};

// Invoked by the CUDA driver thread after all preceding stream work has
// completed. No GIL is held on entry.
//
// The GIL must be acquired before taking ownership of `rawUserData`. The
// `unique_ptr` destructor decrements the contained `nb::object`'s Python
// refcount, which is only legal with the GIL held. Declaring `userData`
// after `gil` guarantees the correct destruction order.
void hostFuncTrampoline(void *rawUserData) {
  nb::gil_scoped_acquire gil;
  std::unique_ptr<HostFuncUserData> userData(
      static_cast<HostFuncUserData *>(rawUserData));
  try {
    userData->fn();
  } catch (nb::python_error &e) {
    e.restore();
    PyErr_Print();
  } catch (const std::exception &e) {
    PySys_WriteStderr("host callback raised C++ exception: %s\n", e.what());
  }
}

} // namespace

void Python::DeviceStream::enqueueHostFunc(nb::callable &&fn) const {
  auto userData =
      std::make_unique<HostFuncUserData>(HostFuncUserData{std::move(fn)});

  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceStreamRef> mlrtStream = stream->ctx->stream();
  if (mlrtStream.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(mlrtStream.getError());

  ErrorOrSuccess err = [&] {
    nb::gil_scoped_release release;
    return (*mlrtStream)->enqueueHostFunc(&hostFuncTrampoline, userData.get());
  }();
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());

  (void)userData.release();
}

std::tuple<uintptr_t, uintptr_t> Python::packHostFunc(nb::callable fn) {
  auto *userData = new HostFuncUserData{std::move(fn)};
  return {reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(&hostFuncTrampoline),
          reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(userData)};
}

namespace {

// CUDA host function. Runs on a CUDA driver thread once the stream
// reaches this node. No GIL on entry. Must return promptly so the
// stream can continue. Dispatches the Python callable onto the
// explicit AsyncRT CPUDevice carried in `userData`, then returns.
//
// The AsyncRT worker re-acquires the GIL, invokes the callable,
// releases the GIL, then signals the flag with `signalValue` (release
// ordering, encapsulated in `CompletionFlag::signal`). A
// `cuStreamWaitValue64` node placed later on the same stream observes
// the value and lets downstream work proceed.
//
// Lifetime split: the outer `AsyncHostFuncUserData` block (which
// includes the `CPUDeviceRef` we dispatch through) is owned by this
// trampoline's stack and freed before returning to CUDA. The inner
// `AsyncHostFuncTaskData` is moved into a separate heap allocation
// owned by the worker closure, so the worker carries only the data it
// actually reads.
void asyncHostFuncTrampoline(void *rawUserData) {
  // Take ownership of the outer block with RAII.
  std::unique_ptr<Python::Detail::AsyncHostFuncUserData> userData(
      static_cast<Python::Detail::AsyncHostFuncUserData *>(rawUserData));

  // Clear the flag before the worker runs. cuStreamWaitValue64 sees 0
  // until the worker calls `signal`.
  userData->task.flagRef->reset();

  // Move the task data into its own heap allocation owned by a
  // shared_ptr with a GIL-aware deleter so the `nb::object`'s
  // Py_DECREF runs under the GIL when the worker finishes.
  auto taskData = std::shared_ptr<Python::Detail::AsyncHostFuncTaskData>(
      new Python::Detail::AsyncHostFuncTaskData(std::move(userData->task)),
      [](Python::Detail::AsyncHostFuncTaskData *p) {
        nb::gil_scoped_acquire gil;
        delete p;
      });

  // Dispatch onto a non-device worker so the callback doesn't contend
  // with the per-GPU command-dispatch worker threads. Outside of cuGraph
  // capture this matters most: a callback that lands on a device-pinned
  // worker can stall GPU command submission. See
  // `MLRT::taskIdForNonDevice`.
  M::AsyncRT::CPUDevice &cpuDevice = *userData->cpuDeviceRef;
  std::size_t numWorkers = cpuDevice.getWorkQueue()->getParallelismLevel();
  M::AsyncRT::addTask(
      cpuDevice,
      [taskData = std::move(taskData)] {
        std::uint64_t value = taskData->signalValue;
        {
          nb::gil_scoped_acquire gil;
          try {
            taskData->fn();
          } catch (nb::python_error &e) {
            e.restore();
            PyErr_Print();
          } catch (const std::exception &e) {
            PySys_WriteStderr("async host callback raised C++ exception: %s\n",
                              e.what());
          }
        } // GIL released here before the signal store.
        // signal() does a release-ordered store: result stores in `fn`
        // are visible before the GPU-side `cuStreamWaitValue64`
        // observes the value.
        taskData->flagRef->signal(value);
      },
      M::MLRT::taskIdForNonDevice(0, numWorkers));
}

} // namespace

void Python::DeviceStream::enqueueAsyncHostFunc(nb::callable &&fn,
                                                const CompletionFlag &flag,
                                                uint64_t value,
                                                const CPU &cpu) const {
  // Eagerly construct the user-data block at enqueue time; the factory
  // pulls `cpu`'s `CPUDeviceRef` and raises a clear Python error if
  // `cpu` is malformed (rather than crashing on a null deref in the
  // trampoline).
  auto userData = cpu.makeAsyncHostFuncUserData(std::move(fn), flag, value);

  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceStreamRef> mlrtStream = stream->ctx->stream();
  if (mlrtStream.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(mlrtStream.getError());

  ErrorOrSuccess err = [&] {
    nb::gil_scoped_release release;
    return (*mlrtStream)
        ->enqueueHostFunc(&asyncHostFuncTrampoline, userData.get());
  }();
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());

  (void)userData.release();
}

void Python::DeviceStream::waitForHostValue(const CompletionFlag &flag,
                                            uint64_t value) const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceStreamRef> mlrtStream = stream->ctx->stream();
  if (mlrtStream.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(mlrtStream.getError());

  ErrorOrSuccess err =
      (*mlrtStream)->enqueueWaitOnHostValue(*flag.ref(), value);
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());
}

void Python::DeviceStream::waitForDevice(const Device &device) const {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOrSuccess err = stream->ctx->enqueueWaitFor(*device.ctx);
  if (err.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(err.getError());
}

uintptr_t Python::DeviceStream::nativeStreamHandle() const {
  // Mirrors getAsString's extraction: ask the device context for its native
  // stream and return the raw pointer. 0 when there is none (e.g. a CPU
  // device), which native callers treat as "no stream". Non-zero means a
  // CUstream / hipStream_t to callers, so other backends report 0.
  M::Driver::Device::API api = stream->ctx->device().api();
  if (api != M::Driver::Device::cudaAPI && api != M::Driver::Device::hipAPI)
    return 0;
  auto err = stream->ctx->stream();
  if (err.isError())
    return 0;
  return reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>((*err)->ptr());
}

Python::PyDeviceTy Python::DeviceStream::getDevice() const { return dev; }

Python::PyDeviceStreamTy Python::DeviceStream::createStream(Device &device) {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceContextRef> newCtx =
      device.ctx->device().createContext();
  if (newCtx.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(newCtx.getError());

  return std::make_unique<DeviceStream>(device, *newCtx);
}

bool Python::DeviceStream::operator==(const DeviceStream &other) const {
  return *this->stream->ctx == *other.stream->ctx;
}

/// Helper to return the Python device object from dlpack device type and id.
std::tuple<std::shared_ptr<Python::Device>, std::optional<intptr_t>>
Python::getPyDevice(DLDeviceType deviceType, ssize_t deviceID) {
  if (deviceType == DLDeviceType::kDLCPU)
    return {Python::getCpuDevice(deviceID), std::nullopt};

  std::shared_ptr<Device> device = Python::getAccelerator(deviceID);
  auto &ctxDev = device->ctx->device();

  if (static_cast<DLDeviceType>(ctxDev.getDLDevice(false).device_type) !=
      deviceType)
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "unsupported device type in dlpack implementation");

  return {device, device->ctx->getDLPackStream()};
}

/// Helper to return the Python device object from a dlpack array.
std::tuple<std::shared_ptr<Python::Device>, std::optional<intptr_t>>
Python::getPyDevice(const nb::object &arrayOrTensor) {
  auto [deviceType, deviceID] = DLPack::callDLPackDevice(arrayOrTensor);
  return getPyDevice(deviceType, deviceID);
}

namespace {
// The accelerator cache stores `weak_ptr`s so that GPU devices can be properly
// released. Otherwise, some resources owned by the device are held too long,
// and can cause segfaults if multiple models are run one after another.
template <class DeviceType>
class WeakDeviceCache {
public:
  std::shared_ptr<DeviceType> find(ssize_t key) {
    // If we have a cache entry that hasn't been freed yet, we just return it.
    if (auto it = map.find(key); it != map.end())
      if (std::shared_ptr<DeviceType> ptr = it->second.lock())
        return ptr;
    return nullptr;
  }

  std::shared_ptr<DeviceType> insert(ssize_t key, M::DeviceSpec spec,
                                     M::Driver::DeviceContextRef ctx) {
    auto shared = std::make_shared<DeviceType>(std::move(spec), std::move(ctx));
    // We use insert_or_assign to overwrite potential freed entries.
    map.insert_or_assign(key, shared);
    return shared;
  }

private:
  llvm::SmallDenseMap<ssize_t, std::weak_ptr<DeviceType>> map;
};

// The CPU cache stores `shared_ptr`s so that CPU devices (and the AsyncRT
// cpuDevice they hold) remain alive for the lifetime of the process.
template <class DeviceType>
class StrongDeviceCache {
public:
  std::shared_ptr<DeviceType> find(ssize_t key) {
    if (auto it = map.find(key); it != map.end())
      return it->second;
    return nullptr;
  }

  std::shared_ptr<DeviceType> insert(ssize_t key, M::DeviceSpec spec,
                                     M::Driver::DeviceContextRef ctx) {
    auto shared = std::make_shared<DeviceType>(std::move(spec), std::move(ctx));
    map.insert_or_assign(key, shared);
    return shared;
  }

private:
  llvm::SmallDenseMap<ssize_t, std::shared_ptr<DeviceType>> map;
};

using CPUCache = StrongDeviceCache<Python::CPU>;
using AcceleratorCache = WeakDeviceCache<Python::Accelerator>;
} // namespace

/// Protects the cache returned by `getCPUCache`.
static std::mutex &getCPUCacheMutex() {
  static std::mutex cacheMutex;
  return cacheMutex;
}

/// Users must acquire the `CPUCacheMutex` first;
static CPUCache &getCPUCache() {
  // Intentionally leaked: the CPU cache holds `shared_ptr<Python::CPU>`, which
  // in turn keeps the AsyncRT cpuDevice alive. At process exit, static-local
  // destructors across translation units run in reverse-of-construction order.
  // The global cpuDevice mutex (in libAsyncRTRuntimeGlobals.dylib) is
  // constructed *after* this cache (on first CpuDeviceContext creation), so it
  // is destroyed *first*. If the cache were then destroyed normally, releasing
  // its shared refs would run `CPUDevice::~Runtime` →
  // `clearGlobalCPUDevicePointerIfEquals`, which locks the already-destroyed
  // mutex — on macOS that returns EINVAL and std::mutex throws, terminating the
  // process (GEX-3583). Leaking the cache matches the stated intent that CPU
  // devices live for the lifetime of the process.
  static CPUCache *cache = new CPUCache{};
  return *cache;
}

namespace {
using DeviceContextPair = std::pair<M::DeviceSpec, M::Driver::DeviceContextRef>;

/// Builds the CPU (spec, context) pair `M_createCPUDevice` used to produce.
/// The spec's id stays 0 for every numa node, matching the wrapper; only the
/// cache keys on the requested id.
ErrorOr<DeviceContextPair> makeCPUDeviceContext() {
  ErrorOr<TargetInfo> targetOr = M::getHostTargetInfo();
  if (targetOr.isError())
    return targetOr.takeError();

  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceContextRef> ctxOr =
      M::Driver::DeviceContext::create(M::Driver::Device::cpuAPI);
  if (ctxOr.isError())
    return ctxOr.takeError();

  M::DeviceSpec spec;
  spec.ref.id = 0;
  spec.ref.label = kCPULabel;
  spec.target = targetOr.takeValue();
  return DeviceContextPair{std::move(spec), ctxOr.takeValue()};
}

/// Builds the accelerator (spec, context) pair `M_createAcceleratorDevice`
/// used to produce.
ErrorOr<DeviceContextPair> makeAcceleratorDeviceContext(ssize_t deviceId) {
  ErrorOr<M::Driver::DeviceContextRef> ctxOr =
      M::Driver::DeviceContext::getOrCreate(M::Driver::Device::gpuAPI,
                                            deviceId >= 0 ? deviceId : 0);
  if (ctxOr.isError())
    return ctxOr.takeError();

  M::DeviceSpec spec;
  spec.ref.label = kGPULabel;
  spec.ref.id = deviceId;
  return DeviceContextPair{std::move(spec), ctxOr.takeValue()};
}
} // namespace

std::shared_ptr<Python::CPU> Python::getCpuDevice(ssize_t numaId) {
  numaId = numaId >= 0 ? numaId : 0;
  CPUCache &cache = getCPUCache();
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getCPUCacheMutex());
    if (auto maybeDevice = cache.find(numaId))
      return maybeDevice;
  }

  ErrorOr<DeviceContextPair> deviceOr = [&] {
    nb::gil_scoped_release release;
    return makeCPUDeviceContext();
  }();
  if (deviceOr.isError()) {
    std::string errorMessage =
        "failed to create device: "s + deviceOr.getError();
    throw std::invalid_argument(errorMessage);
  }
  DeviceContextPair created = deviceOr.takeValue();

  ErrorOrSuccess compatibleOr = [&] {
    nb::gil_scoped_release release;
    return created.second->device().isCompatible();
  }();
  if (compatibleOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(compatibleOr.getError());

  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getCPUCacheMutex());
  return cache.insert(numaId, std::move(created.first),
                      std::move(created.second));
}

/// Protects the cache returned by `getAcceleratorCache`.
static std::mutex &getAcceleratorCacheMutex() {
  static std::mutex cacheMutex;
  return cacheMutex;
}

/// Users must acquire the `acceleratorCacheMutex` first;
static AcceleratorCache &getAcceleratorCache() {
  static AcceleratorCache cache{};
  return cache;
}

std::shared_ptr<Python::Accelerator> Python::getAccelerator(ssize_t gpuId) {
  gpuId = gpuId >= 0 ? gpuId : 0;
  AcceleratorCache &cache = getAcceleratorCache();
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getAcceleratorCacheMutex());
    if (auto maybeDevice = cache.find(gpuId))
      return maybeDevice;
  }

  ErrorOr<DeviceContextPair> deviceOr = [&] {
    nb::gil_scoped_release release;
    return makeAcceleratorDeviceContext(gpuId);
  }();
  if (deviceOr.isError()) {
    std::string errorMessage =
        "failed to create device: "s + deviceOr.getError();
    throw std::invalid_argument(errorMessage);
  }
  DeviceContextPair created = deviceOr.takeValue();

  ErrorOrSuccess compatibleOr = [&] {
    nb::gil_scoped_release release;
    return created.second->device().isCompatible();
  }();
  if (compatibleOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(compatibleOr.getError());

  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getAcceleratorCacheMutex());
  return cache.insert(gpuId, std::move(created.first),
                      std::move(created.second));
}

// Returns number of accelerators available.
int Python::acceleratorCount() {
  nb::gil_scoped_release release;
  return M::Driver::Device::numberOfDevices(M::Driver::Device::gpuAPI);
}

size_t Python::Device::hash() const {
  std::size_t h1 = std::hash<std::string>{}(this->getLabel());
  std::size_t h2 = std::hash<uint64_t>{}(this->getId());
  return h1 ^ (h2 << 1);
}

#include "AsyncRT/Runtime/Algorithms.h"

#define CHECK_IS_CPU_ERR(dev)                                                  \
  do {                                                                         \
    if ((dev).api() != Device::cpuAPI) {                                       \
      RETURN_ERROR("Not a CPU device.");                                       \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

#ifdef _WIN32

ErrorOr<Device::MemInfo> CpuDevice::getMemoryInfo() const {
  MEMORYSTATUSEX status;
  status.dwLength = sizeof(status);
  if (!GlobalMemoryStatusEx(&status))
    RETURN_ERROR("Failed to get memory status via GlobalMemoryStatusEx");
  Device::MemInfo info;
  info.total = status.ullTotalPhys;
  info.free = status.ullAvailPhys;
  return info;
}

#else // _WIN32

// Call sysconf() and check for errors.
static ErrorOr<size_t> getSystemValue(int name) {
  errno = 0;
  auto value = sysconf(name);
  if (errno != 0)
    RETURN_ERROR(strerror(errno));
  return static_cast<size_t>(value);
}

ErrorOr<Device::MemInfo> CpuDevice::getMemoryInfo() const {
  Device::MemInfo info;
  auto numPages = getSystemValue(_SC_PHYS_PAGES);
  if (numPages.isError())
    return numPages.takeError();
  auto pageSize = getSystemValue(_SC_PAGE_SIZE);
  if (pageSize.isError())
    return pageSize.takeError();

  rusage usage;
  if (-1 == getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &usage))
    RETURN_ERROR("Failed to get current memory usage via rusage");

// The unit for the _SC_PAGE_SIZE is bytes. The unit for the ru_maxrss is
// kilobytes on Linux and bytes on MacOS.
#if MODULAR_LINUX
  const size_t maxrssMultiple = 1024;
#else // macOS
  const size_t maxrssMultiple = 1;
#endif

  // This is the maximum resident set size used.
  // Current memory use may be lower, this is the "high water mark".
  size_t used = usage.ru_maxrss * maxrssMultiple;
  // Total memory = number of pages times the page size.
  info.total = numPages.takeValue() * pageSize.takeValue();
  // Free memory = total memory minus memory in use.
  info.free = info.total - used;
  return info;
}

#endif // _WIN32

//
// ===== CpuDeviceContext === //
//
CpuDeviceContext::CpuDeviceContext(CpuDevice &device)
    : DeviceContext(device, TypeID::get<CpuDeviceContext>()) {
  // Get or create the cpuDevice. Request mainWillDonate=false if this is the
  // only cpuDevice user, but allow using the existing cpuDevice options if they
  // are set. This is safe as the other cpuDevice users are guaranteeing they
  // will wait on the main thread to progress work. Otherwise CpuDeviceContext
  // is invariant to the cpuDevice options, so this is safe.
  cpuDevice = AsyncRT::getOrCreateCPUDevice(
      AsyncRT::CPUDeviceSource::CPUDeviceContext,
      AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions().withMainWillNotDonate(),
      /*allowUsingExistingOptions=*/true);

  streamChain = cpuDevice->getReadyChain().copy();
}

CpuDeviceContext::~CpuDeviceContext() {
  // Wait for pending work to finish
  if (!streamChain.isReady())
    cpuDevice->getWorkQueue()->await({&streamChain, 1});
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::memAlloc(void **ptr, size_t byteSize,
                                          Device::AllocMode mode) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::memAlloc", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  assert(byteSize != 0);
  *ptr = cpuDevice->getAllocator()->allocateBytes(byteSize, /*alignment=*/1);
  if (*ptr == nullptr) {
    RETURN_ERROR("Memory allocation failed");
  }
  return success();
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::memFree(void *ptr, Device::FreeKind kind) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::memFree", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  // A CPU device's allocations are already host memory; nothing to wrap.
  if (kind == Device::FreeKind::WRAPPED)
    RETURN_ERROR("CpuDeviceContext::memFree: WRAPPED memory is not supported");
  // The Runtime's allocator outlives any work enqueued on its work queue, so
  // capturing a raw pointer here (rather than a CPUDeviceRef) is safe.
  auto *allocator = cpuDevice->getAllocator();
  if (kind == Device::FreeKind::HOST) {
    allocator->deallocateBytes(ptr);
    return success();
  }
  return enqueueWork([=]() { allocator->deallocateBytes(ptr); });
}

void *CpuDeviceContext::driverContext() const { return nullptr; }

// Enqueue work with stream-like semantics. Keep a chain to the last enqueued
// function so the next task can await it.
// Returns any pending error from previously enqueued async work.
ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueWork(AsyncRT::TaskFunction &&work) {
  RETURN_IF_PENDING_ERROR(*this);

  auto eventChain =
      AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<AsyncRT::Chain>::allocate(*cpuDevice);

  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> streamLock{streamChainMutex};
  streamChain.andThenAsync(
      [work = std::move(work), eventChain = eventChain.copy()]() mutable {
        work();
        std::move(eventChain).emplace();
      });
  streamChain = std::move(eventChain);
  return success();
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueCopyToDevice(void *dst, const void *src,
                                                     size_t byteSize) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueCopyToDevice",
                       TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  return enqueueWork([=]() { memcpy(dst, src, byteSize); });
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueCopyFromDevice(void *dst,
                                                       const void *src,
                                                       size_t byteSize) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueCopyFromDevice",
                       TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  return enqueueWork([=]() { memcpy(dst, src, byteSize); });
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::memCopyDtoD(DeviceBuffer &dst,
                                             DeviceBuffer &src,
                                             size_t srcByteOffset,
                                             size_t srcByteSize,
                                             bool /*crossStreamSync*/) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::memCopyDtoD", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  CHECK_IS_CPU_ERR(src.context().device());
  CHECK_IS_CPU_ERR(dst.context().device());
  void *srcPtr = (uint8_t *)src.ptr() + srcByteOffset;
  void *dstPtr = dst.ptr();
  size_t size = dst.byteSize();
  assert(srcByteOffset + srcByteSize <= src.byteSize());
  assert(srcByteSize == dst.byteSize());
  return enqueueWork([=]() { memcpy(dstPtr, srcPtr, size); });
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueSetMemory(void *dst, size_t byteSize,
                                                  uint64_t val,
                                                  size_t valSize) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueSetMemory",
                       TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);

  if (valSize > sizeof(uint64_t))
    return Error("unsupported val size");

  if (valSize != 1 && (byteSize & (valSize - 1)))
    return Error("byteSize of buffer is misaligned");

  return enqueueWork([this, dst, byteSize, val, valSize]() {
    size_t len = byteSize / valSize;
    switch (valSize) {
    case 1: {
      uint8_t u8Val = static_cast<uint8_t>(val);
      RECORD_PENDING_ERROR(*this,
                           M::fillHomogeneous(dst, len, DType::ui8, &u8Val));
      break;
    }
    case 2: {
      uint16_t ui16Val = static_cast<uint16_t>(val);
      RECORD_PENDING_ERROR(*this,
                           M::fillHomogeneous(dst, len, DType::ui16, &ui16Val));
      break;
    }
    case 4: {
      uint32_t ui32Val = static_cast<uint32_t>(val);
      RECORD_PENDING_ERROR(*this,
                           M::fillHomogeneous(dst, len, DType::ui32, &ui32Val));
      break;
    }
    case 8: {
      uint64_t ui64Val = static_cast<uint64_t>(val);
      RECORD_PENDING_ERROR(*this,
                           M::fillHomogeneous(dst, len, DType::ui64, &ui64Val));
      break;
    }
    default:
      llvm_unreachable("unsupported val size");
    }
  });
}

DeviceContext::MMapFileImplResult
CpuDeviceContext::memmapFileImpl(const std::filesystem::path &filename) const {
  auto result = openFile(filename, /*readOnly*/ true);
  if (result)
    return result.takeError();
  auto [fd, status] = *result;

  auto size = status.getSize();

  std::error_code ec;
  llvm::sys::fs::mapped_file_region mappedFile(
      fd, llvm::sys::fs::mapped_file_region::readonly, size, 0, ec);
  if (ec) {
    llvm::sys::fs::closeFile(fd);
    return Error(ec.message());
  }

  // Close the file, mmap will hold a ref to the descriptor.
  llvm::sys::fs::closeFile(fd);

  return std::tuple{
      mappedFile.data(),
      size,
      std::optional{std::move(mappedFile)},
  };
}

ErrorOrSuccess
CpuDeviceContext::enqueueHostFunction(void (*resumeFunc)(int8_t *),
                                      void (*destroyFunc)(int8_t *),
                                      int8_t *coroHandle) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueHostFunction",
                       TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  // Resume the coroutine to execute the enqueued function, then immediately
  // destroy the coroutine as ownership of it has been transferred from Mojo by
  // this point.
  return enqueueWork([=]() {
    resumeFunc(coroHandle);
    destroyFunc(coroHandle);
  });
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueHostFunctionRange(
    void (*resumeFunc)(int8_t *), void (*destroyFunc)(int8_t *),
    int8_t **coroHandles, size_t numHandles) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueHostFunctionRange",
                       TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  RETURN_IF_PENDING_ERROR(*this);

  if (numHandles == 0)
    return success();

  size_t numWorkers = cpuDevice->getWorkQueue()->getParallelismLevel();
  auto eventChain =
      AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<AsyncRT::Chain>::allocate(*cpuDevice);
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> streamLock{streamChainMutex};

  // When the current streamChain is ready, fan out all coroutine handles
  // across worker threads via parallelForEachNChainWithTaskIds, then
  // complete eventChain when all handles have been processed.
  // Copy the handles array since it may not outlive this call. Use a plain
  // std::vector as we will typically have one handle per CPU thread which is
  // too big for SmallVector.
  streamChain.andThenSync([cpuDevice = this->cpuDevice, numWorkers, resumeFunc,
                           destroyFunc, eventChain = eventChain.copy(),
                           handles = std::vector<int8_t *>(
                               coroHandles,
                               coroHandles + numHandles)]() mutable {
    size_t count = handles.size();
    auto completionChain = AsyncRT::parallelForEachNChainWithTaskIds(
        *cpuDevice, count,
        [numWorkers](size_t i) -> int {
          return static_cast<int>(i % numWorkers);
        },
        [resumeFunc, destroyFunc](size_t i, std::vector<int8_t *> &handles) {
          resumeFunc(handles[i]);
          destroyFunc(handles[i]);
        },
        std::move(handles));
    completionChain.andThenSync([eventChain = std::move(eventChain)]() mutable {
      std::move(eventChain).emplace();
    });
  });

  streamChain = std::move(eventChain);
  return success();
}

ErrorOr<DeviceStreamRef> CpuDeviceContext::stream() const {
  // This function is const only for the duration of its execution;
  // `this` is non-const downstream so cast in order to provide
  // mutable reference to the new stream object.
  return CpuDeviceStreamRef::create(const_cast<CpuDeviceContext &>(*this));
}

CpuDeviceContext::createExternalStream(void *externalStream) {

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::synchronize() {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::synchronize", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  RETURN_IF_PENDING_ERROR(*this);
  AsyncRT::AnyAsyncValueRef head;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> streamLock{streamChainMutex};
    head = streamChain.copy();
  }
  cpuDevice->getWorkQueue()->await({&head, 1});
  RETURN_IF_ERROR(pollPendingEvents());
  return checkPendingError();
}

ErrorOr<DeviceEventRef> CpuDeviceContext::enqueueEvent() {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueEvent", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> streamLock{streamChainMutex};
  return CpuDeviceEventRef::create(static_cast<CpuDevice &>(device()),
                                   cpuDevice, streamChain.copy());
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueEvent(const DeviceEvent &event) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueEvent", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  auto &cpuEvent =
      const_cast<CpuDeviceEvent &>(static_cast<const CpuDeviceEvent &>(event));
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> streamLock{streamChainMutex};
  cpuEvent.asyncValue() = streamChain.copy();
  return success();
}

ErrorOr<DeviceEventRef> CpuDeviceContext::eventCreate(bool enableTiming) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::eventCreate", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  return CpuDeviceEventRef::create(static_cast<CpuDevice &>(device()),
                                   cpuDevice,
                                   cpuDevice->getReadyChain().copy());
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueWaitFor(DeviceEvent &event) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueWaitFor", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  RETURN_IF_PENDING_ERROR(*this);

  auto &cpuEvent = static_cast<CpuDeviceEvent &>(event);
  auto eventChain =
      AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<AsyncRT::Chain>::allocate(*cpuDevice);

  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> streamLock{streamChainMutex};
  AsyncRT::andThenAsync(
      std::make_tuple(streamChain.copy(), cpuEvent.asyncValue().copy()),
      [eventChain = eventChain.copy()](auto, auto) mutable {
        std::move(eventChain).emplace();
      });
  streamChain = std::move(eventChain);
  return success();
}

ErrorOrSuccess CpuDeviceContext::enqueueWaitFor(DeviceContext &ctx) {
  TRACY_ZONE_SCOPED_NC("CpuDeviceContext::enqueueWaitFor", TRACY_COLOR_PURPLE);
  RETURN_IF_PENDING_ERROR(*this);

  auto &other = static_cast<CpuDeviceContext &>(ctx);
  auto eventChain =
      AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<AsyncRT::Chain>::allocate(*cpuDevice);

  std::scoped_lock<std::mutex, std::mutex> lock{streamChainMutex,
                                                other.streamChainMutex};
  AsyncRT::andThenAsync(
      std::make_tuple(streamChain.copy(), other.streamChain.copy()),
      [eventChain = eventChain.copy()](auto, auto) mutable {
        std::move(eventChain).emplace();
      });
  streamChain = std::move(eventChain);
  return success();
}

ErrorOr<DeviceTimerRef> CpuDeviceContext::startTimer() {
  return CpuDeviceTimerRef::create(*this, std::chrono::steady_clock::now());
}

ErrorOr<std::chrono::nanoseconds>
CpuDeviceContext::stopTimer(const DeviceTimer &timer) {
  return std::chrono::steady_clock::now() -
         CpuDeviceTimer::cast(timer).cpu_start();
}

ErrorOr<int> CpuDeviceContext::getAttribute(Attribute attr) const {
  switch (attr) {
  case Attribute::PARALLELISM_LEVEL:
    return static_cast<int>(cpuDevice->getWorkQueue()->getParallelismLevel());
  }
  RETURN_ERROR("Unsupported CpuDeviceContext attribute");
}

ErrorOr<Device::MemInfo> CpuDeviceContext::getDeviceMemoryInfo() const {
  return device().getMemoryInfo();
}

ErrorOr<void *>
CpuDeviceContext::getHostAccessiblePointer(const void *devicePtr) {
  if (devicePtr == nullptr)
    RETURN_ERROR("getHostAccessiblePointer: pointer is null");
  return const_cast<void *>(devicePtr);
}

CpuDeviceContext::cast(const DeviceContext &ctx) {
  return DeviceContext::cast<CpuDeviceContext>(ctx);
}

template <typename T>
static void setMojoDefine(M::Core::InferenceSession &self, const char *key,
                          T value) {
  auto &ctx = self.getRuntimeContext().maxContext;
  auto &options = ctx->emplaceIfMissing<KGEN::CompilationContext>();
  options.mojoDefines[key] = value;
}

void M::Graph::Python::bindEngineModule(nb::module_ m) {
  m.doc() = R"nbdoc(
        Modular framework Python bindings.
    )nbdoc";

  nb::class_<ModelTensorSpec>(m, "TensorSpec", R"nbdoc(
        Defines the properties of a tensor, including its name, shape and data type.

        For usage examples, see :obj:`Model.input_metadata`.
      )nbdoc")
      // Properties
      .def_prop_ro(
          "dtype",
          [](ModelTensorSpec &self) { return self.getSpec().getEltType(); },
          "A tensor data type.")
      .def_prop_ro("name", &ModelTensorSpec::getName, "A tensor name.")
      .def_prop_ro(
          "shape",
          [](ModelTensorSpec &self)
              -> std::optional<std::vector<std::optional<std::size_t>>> {
            const auto &spec = self.getSpec();
            if (!spec.hasRank())
              return std::nullopt;

            std::vector<std::optional<std::size_t>> result;
            result.reserve(spec.getRank());
            for (const auto dim : spec) {
              if (dim < 0)
                result.push_back(std::nullopt);
              else
                result.push_back(dim);
            }
            return result;
          },
          R"nbdoc(
        The shape of the tensor as a list of integers.

        If a dimension size is unknown/dynamic (such as the batch size), its
        value is ``None``.
      )nbdoc")
      // Dunders
      .def("__repr__",
           [](ModelTensorSpec &) -> nb::str {
             return {}; /* Replaced in Python*/
           })
      .def("__str__", [](ModelTensorSpec &) -> nb::str {
        return {}; /* Replaced in Python*/
      });

  nb::class_<M::CompiledModels>(m, "CompiledModels", R"nbdoc(
        A compiled model artifact containing one or more submodels.
      )nbdoc")
      .def("__len__",
           [](const M::CompiledModels &self) { return self.getNumModels(); })
      .def(
          "__getitem__",
          [](const M::CompiledModels &self, ssize_t index) -> const M::Model * {
            ssize_t numModels = static_cast<ssize_t>(self.getNumModels());
            if (index < 0)
              index += numModels;
            if (index < 0 || index >= numModels)
              throw nb::index_error();
            return self.getModel(static_cast<size_t>(index));
          },
          nb::rv_policy::reference, nb::keep_alive<0, 1>())
      .def("__iter__",
           [](const M::CompiledModels &self) {
             auto models =
                 llvm::map_range(self.getModels(),
                                 [](const std::unique_ptr<const M::Model> &m) {
                                   return m.get();
                                 });
             return nb::make_iterator<nb::rv_policy::reference_internal>(
                 nb::type<M::CompiledModels>(), "CompiledModelsIterator",
                 models.begin(), models.end());
           })
      .def_prop_ro("names",
                   [](const M::CompiledModels &self) {
                     return llvm::map_to_vector(
                         self.getModels(),
                         [](const std::unique_ptr<const M::Model> &m) {
                           return m->getName().str();
                         });
                   })
      .def(
          "export_mef",
          [](M::CompiledModels &self, const char *path) {
            BufferRef buffer = self.getBuffer();
            if (!buffer)
              throw std::invalid_argument(
                  "compiled model buffer is not available");
            // TODO MSDK-1026: Delete the `remove` call below.
            // Remove the file if it exists. Currently, getFile maps the file
            // to be written to. But if the new content is shorter than the
            // original file content, there will be leftover data from the old
            // version. A better fix is to provide a createFile in
            // WriteableBuffer.
            (void)llvm::sys::fs::remove(path);
            auto writeOr =
                WriteableBuffer::getFile(path, buffer->getBufferSize(), 0);
            if (writeOr.isError())
              throw std::invalid_argument(writeOr.getError());
            WriteableBufferRef os = writeOr.takeValue();
            *os << buffer->getBuffer();
          },
          "path"_a,
          R"nbdoc(
        Exports the compiled model as MEF bytes to the given file.

        Args:
            path: The filesystem path to write the MEF to.
      )nbdoc");

  m.def(
      "get_config_value",
      [](const std::string &key) -> std::string {
        auto configOr = M::Config::open();
        if (configOr.isError())
          throw std::runtime_error(configOr.getError());
        std::optional<llvm::StringRef> value = configOr->maybeGetValue(key);
        if (!value)
          throw nb::key_error(key.c_str());
        return value->str();
      },
      "key"_a,
      R"nbdoc(
      Reads a config value.

      Global overrides take priority, then the ``MODULAR_<KEY>``
      environment variable, then ``modular.cfg``.

      Raises:
          KeyError: If the key is not set in any source.
          RuntimeError: If the config fails to open.
      )nbdoc");
  m.def(
      "get_global_value",
      [](const std::string &key) -> std::optional<std::string> {
        return M::Config::getGlobalValueIfSet(key);
      },
      "key"_a,
      R"nbdoc(
      Returns the process-wide override for ``key``, or ``None`` if unset.

      Ignores environment variables and ``modular.cfg``.
      )nbdoc");
  m.def(
      "set_global_value",
      [](const std::string &key, const std::string &value) {
        M::Config::setGlobalValue(key, value);
      },
      "key"_a, "value"_a,
      R"nbdoc(
      Sets a process-wide config override.

      Overrides take priority over environment variables and
      ``modular.cfg`` for every consumer in the process. They are not
      inherited by subprocesses.
      )nbdoc");
  m.def(
      "unset_global_value",
      [](const std::string &key) { M::Config::unsetGlobalValue(key); }, "key"_a,
      R"nbdoc(
      Removes an override set by :func:`set_global_value`.
      )nbdoc");
  m.def(
      "max_cache_dir",
      []() -> std::optional<std::filesystem::path> {
        return M::getMaxCacheDir();
      },
      R"nbdoc(
      Returns the directory the engine caches compiled models (``.mef``) in.

      Resolved by the compiler itself.

      Returns:
          pathlib.Path | None: the cache directory, or None if unresolvable.
    )nbdoc");

  m.def(
       "read",
       [](std::filesystem::path path) {
         nb::gil_scoped_release release;
         auto bufferOr = M::Buffer::getFile(path);
         if (bufferOr.isError())
           throw std::runtime_error(bufferOr.getError());
         auto modelsOr = M::CompiledModels::read(bufferOr.takeValue());
         if (modelsOr.isError())
           throw std::runtime_error(modelsOr.getError());
         return modelsOr.takeValue();
       },
       "path"_a,
       R"nbdoc(
      Reads a compiled-model artifact (``.mef``) from a file path.

      Returns:
          The artifact, ready to be initialized on any session via
          ``InferenceSession._load_all``.

      Raises:
          RuntimeError: If the file is missing or is not a valid MEF
              for this engine build.
      )nbdoc")
      .def(
          "read",
          [](nb::bytes data) {
            // Copy into an attribute-aligned owning buffer while the GIL
            // still pins `data`; MEF sections require maxAttributeAlignment
            // and Python bytes make no alignment promise.
            auto buffer = M::WriteableBuffer::get(
                data.size(), M::maxAttributeAlignment().value());
            std::memcpy(buffer->getBufferStart(), data.c_str(), data.size());
            nb::gil_scoped_release release;
            auto modelsOr = M::CompiledModels::read(std::move(buffer));
            if (modelsOr.isError())
              throw std::runtime_error(modelsOr.getError());
            return modelsOr.takeValue();
          },
          "data"_a,
          R"nbdoc(
      Reads a compiled-model artifact (``.mef``) from bytes.

      Returns:
          The artifact, ready to be initialized on any session via
          ``InferenceSession._load_all``.

      Raises:
          RuntimeError: If the bytes are not a valid MEF for this
              engine build.
      )nbdoc");

  nb::class_<M::Core::ModelHandle>(m, "Model", R"nbdoc(
        A loaded model that you can execute.

        Do not instantiate this class directly. Instead, create it with
        :meth:`InferenceSession.load` or :meth:`InferenceSession.init`.

        A :class:`Model` is callable. Calling it directly (``model(inputs...)``)
        accepts tensors as positional or keyword arguments and dispatches
        to :meth:`execute`. You can also call :meth:`execute` directly, which
        accepts positional arguments only.

        When using keyword arguments, the names must match the model's input
        metadata (see :attr:`input_metadata`). Calling the model raises
        ``TypeError`` if a keyword argument doesn't match a model input, if a
        positional and keyword argument refer to the same parameter, or if the
        number of inputs doesn't match.

        For supported input types and execution errors, see :meth:`execute`.

        For example, load a graph, list its inputs, and run it:

        .. code-block:: python

            import numpy as np

            from max.driver import CPU
            from max.dtype import DType
            from max.engine import InferenceSession
            from max.graph import DeviceRef, Graph, TensorType

            with Graph(
                "add_one",
                input_types=[
                    TensorType(DType.float32, ["batch"], device=DeviceRef.CPU())
                ],
            ) as graph:
                (x,) = graph.inputs
                graph.output(x + 1.0)

            session = InferenceSession(devices=[CPU()])
            model = session.load(graph)
            for tensor in model.input_metadata:
                print(
                    f"name: {tensor.name}, shape: {tensor.shape},"
                    f" dtype: {tensor.dtype}"
                )
            outputs = model.execute(np.ones((2,), np.float32))
      )nbdoc")

                   "The device objects used by the model.")
      .def_ro("input_devices", &M::Core::ModelHandle::inputDevicesPy,

      .def_prop_ro("input_metadata", &M::Core::ModelHandle::getInputMetadata,

        Metadata about the model's input tensors, as a list of :class:`TensorSpec` objects.

        For example, you can print the input tensor names, shapes, and dtypes:

        .. code-block:: python

            from max.driver import CPU
            from max.dtype import DType
            from max.engine import InferenceSession
            from max.graph import DeviceRef, Graph, TensorType

            device = CPU()
            device_ref = DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            input_type = TensorType(DType.float32, [2, 3], device=device_ref)
            with Graph("metadata", input_types=[input_type]) as graph:
                graph.output(graph.inputs[0])

            session = InferenceSession(devices=[device])
            model = session.load(graph)
            for tensor in model.input_metadata:
                print(f'name: {tensor.name}, shape: {tensor.shape}, dtype: {tensor.dtype}')
      )nbdoc")

      .def_prop_ro("kernel_summaries",

      .def_prop_ro("name", &M::Core::ModelHandle::getName,

        The symbol name of this model.

        :meth:`InferenceSession.load_all` to key the returned dict by graph

      .def_prop_ro(
          "signature", [](M::Core::ModelHandle &) { /* Replaced in Python */ },
          nb::sig("def signature(self) -> inspect.Signature"),

      // Methods
      .def(
          "execute", [](M::Core::ModelHandle &) { /* Replaced in Python */ },
          nb::sig("def execute(self, *args: InputType) -> list[Buffer]"),
          R"nbdoc(
        Executes the model with the provided input and returns the outputs.

        For example, compiling a small graph and executing it:

        .. code-block:: python

            from max.driver import CPU
            from max.dtype import DType
            from max.engine import InferenceSession
            from max.graph import DeviceRef, Graph, ops

            device = CPU()
            device_ref = DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            with Graph("add") as graph:
                graph.output(
                    ops.add(
                        ops.constant([1.0, 2.0], DType.float32, device=device_ref),
                        ops.constant([3.0, 4.0], DType.float32, device=device_ref),
                    )
                )

            session = InferenceSession(devices=[device])
            model = session.load(graph)
            result = model.execute()[0]

        .. invisible-code-block: python

            import numpy as np

            np.testing.assert_allclose(result.to_numpy(), [4.0, 6.0])

        Args:
            args: A list of input tensors. The following input types are
              supported:

              * Any tensors implementing the DLPack protocol, such as
                :obj:`np.ndarray` or :obj:`torch.Tensor`.
              * MAX driver buffers, such as :obj:`max.driver.Buffer`.
              * Scalar inputs, such as :obj:`bool`, :obj:`float`, :obj:`int`,
                or :obj:`np.generic`.

              All inputs are copied to the device that the model is resident on
              prior to executing.

        Returns:
            A list of output tensors. The output tensors are resident on the
            execution device.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If the given input tensors' shapes don't match what
              the model expects.

            TypeError: If the given input tensors' dtype can't be cast to what
              the model expects.

            ValueError: If positional inputs aren't one of the supported

      )nbdoc")

        Capture is best-effort and model-dependent. It records the current

      .def(

  nb::class_<M::Core::DebugConfig>(m, "DebugConfig", R"nbdoc(
       Unified debug configuration for MAX inference.

       ``DebugConfig`` is a process-wide singleton accessed through
       :attr:`InferenceSession.debug`. It controls model debugging features
       such as ``NaN`` checks, synchronous GPU execution, stack traces, and IR
       dumping.

       There are two ways to configure debugging options:

       * Set the ``MODULAR_DEBUG`` environment variable to a list of
         kebab-case property names separated by commas. Boolean properties
         can be enabled with just the name; others use ``name=value`` form.
         For example: ``MODULAR_DEBUG=nan-check,assert-level=all``.
       * Set properties directly with the Python API, for example
         ``InferenceSession.debug.<property> = <value>``. Options are
         class-level on :class:`InferenceSession` because they affect
         globally shared infrastructure.

       For the environment variable and config file, the name ``sensible``
       enables a curated default set defined in :attr:`sensible_mode`.
      )nbdoc")
      .def_prop_rw("nan_check", &M::Core::DebugConfig::getNanCheck,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setNanCheck,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, triggers MAX to "
                   "insert runtime checks after each compiled op that "
                   "abort if any output contains ``NaN``. Takes effect "
                   "at model build time.")
      .def_prop_rw("uninitialized_read_check",
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::getUninitializedReadCheck,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setUninitializedReadCheck,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, triggers MAX to "
                   "instrument buffer reads to detect reads of "
                   "uninitialized memory. Takes effect at model build "
                   "time.")
      .def_prop_rw("uninitialized_read_mode",
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::getUninitializedReadMode,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setUninitializedReadMode,
                   "A string that sets what :attr:`uninitialized_read_check` "
                   "does on a match. One of ``''``, ``'abort'``, "
                   "``'report'``. ``''`` (unset) behaves as ``'abort'``, "
                   "which stops at the first match. ``'report'`` prints each "
                   "match and keeps running so a single run enumerates every "
                   "offending load, with no bound on its output. On Apple "
                   "GPUs, ``'report'`` currently aborts at the first match "
                   "without printing. Ignored unless "
                   ":attr:`uninitialized_read_check` is set. Takes effect at "
                   "model build time.")
      .def_prop_rw("device_sync_mode", &M::Core::DebugConfig::getDeviceSyncMode,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setDeviceSyncMode,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, triggers MAX to "
                   "force synchronous GPU execution so every device "
                   "operation waits for completion. This surfaces async "
                   "errors at their call site but serializes the "
                   "pipeline. Takes effect at run time.")
      .def_prop_rw("stack_trace_on_error",
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::getStackTraceOnError,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setStackTraceOnError,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, triggers MAX to "
                   "print a C++ stack trace whenever a runtime error "
                   "is raised. Takes effect at run time.")
      .def_prop_rw("stack_trace_on_crash",
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::getStackTraceOnCrash,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setStackTraceOnCrash,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, triggers MAX to "
                   "print a C++ stack trace on fatal signals such as "
                   "``SIGSEGV`` or ``SIGABRT``. Takes effect at run time.")
      .def_prop_rw("source_tracebacks",
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::getSourceTracebacks,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setSourceTracebacks,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, triggers MAX to "
                   "capture Python source locations during graph "
                   "construction so runtime errors can be traced back "
                   "to user code. Takes effect at graph build time "
                   "and is typically set using "
                   "``Graph.debug.source_tracebacks``.")
      .def_prop_rw("pre_jit", &M::Core::DebugConfig::getPreJit,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setPreJit,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, stops graph "
                   "compilation once the Mojo for the graph has been "
                   "emitted (see ``ir_output_dir``), skipping the kernel "
                   "JIT. ``InferenceSession.compile`` then raises "
                   ":class:`~max.engine.CompilationStopped`. Takes "
                   "effect at model build time.")
      .def_prop_rw("op_log_level", &M::Core::DebugConfig::getOpLogLevel,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setOpLogLevel,
                   "A string that sets the log level for per-op "
                   "tracing. One of ``''``, ``'NOTSET'``, ``'TRACE'``, "
                   "``'DEBUG'``, ``'INFO'``, ``'WARNING'``, "
                   "``'ERROR'``, ``'CRITICAL'``. Takes effect at "
                   "model build time.")
      .def_prop_rw("assert_level", &M::Core::DebugConfig::getAssertLevel,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setAssertLevel,
                   "A string that sets the Mojo assertion level for "
                   "compiled kernels. One of ``''``, ``'none'``, "
                   "``'warn'``, ``'safe'``, ``'all'``. Higher levels "
                   "enable more runtime checks at a performance cost. "
                   "Takes effect at "
                   "model build time.")
      .def_prop_rw(
          "print_style",
          [](const M::Core::DebugConfig &self) -> ResultOutputStyle {
            const std::string s = self.getPrintStyle();
            if (s == "compact")
              return ResultOutputStyle::kCompact;
            if (s == "full")
              return ResultOutputStyle::kFull;
            if (s == "binary")
              return ResultOutputStyle::kBinary;
            if (s == "binary_max_checkpoint")
              return ResultOutputStyle::kBinaryMaxCheckpoint;
            return ResultOutputStyle::kNone;
          },
          [](M::Core::DebugConfig &self, ResultOutputStyle v) {
            switch (v) {
            case ResultOutputStyle::kCompact:
              self.setPrintStyle("compact");
              return;
            case ResultOutputStyle::kFull:
              self.setPrintStyle("full");
              return;
            case ResultOutputStyle::kBinary:
              self.setPrintStyle("binary");
              return;
            case ResultOutputStyle::kBinaryMaxCheckpoint:
              self.setPrintStyle("binary_max_checkpoint");
              return;
            case ResultOutputStyle::kNone:
              self.setPrintStyle("none");
              return;
            }
          },
          "A :class:`PrintStyle` value that sets the format for tensor "
          "debug printing. Takes effect at run time.")
      .def_prop_rw("ir_output_dir", &M::Core::DebugConfig::getIrOutputDir,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setIrOutputDir,
                   "A string path to the directory into which MAX "
                   "dumps intermediate compiler IR for inspection. "
                   "Empty string disables dumping. Takes effect at "
                   "model build time.")
      .def_prop_rw("sensible_mode", &M::Core::DebugConfig::getSensibleMode,
                   &M::Core::DebugConfig::setSensibleMode,
                   "A boolean that, when ``True``, triggers MAX to enable a "
                   "curated default debugging set, including ``nan_check``, "
                   "``assert_level='all'``, ``device_sync_mode``, "
                   "``stack_trace_on_error``, ``stack_trace_on_crash``, and "
                   "``source_tracebacks``. You can override the defaults using "
                   "individual properties.")
      .def("reset", &M::Core::DebugConfig::reset,
           "Resets all debug options to their defaults.");

  // InferenceSession is intrusively reference counted, allowing a single
  // reference count between C++ and Python. This requires a bit of additional
  // setup, see
  // https://nanobind.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ownership_adv.html#intrusive-reference-counting
  nb::class_<M::Core::InferenceSession>(
      m, "InferenceSession",
      nb::intrusive_ptr<M::Core::InferenceSession>(
          [](M::Core::InferenceSession *d, PyObject *po) noexcept {
            d->set_self_py(po);
          }),
      R"nbdoc(
      Manages compilation and execution of MAX models.

      An inference session holds device configuration and compiles graphs
      into executable :class:`Model` objects. It also manages custom
      extensions and debug options.

      .. code-block:: python

          from max import driver
          from max._core.engine import InferenceSession

          devices = [driver.CPU()]
          session = InferenceSession(devices, custom_extensions=[])

      Args:
          devices: The devices used for compilation and execution.
          custom_extensions: The paths to custom Mojo extension libraries.
          num_threads: The number of execution threads. Defaults to 0,
              which lets the runtime choose automatically.
  )nbdoc")
      .def(nb::init<std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> &&,
                    std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&, size_t>(),
           "devices"_a, "custom_extensions"_a, "num_threads"_a = 0)
      .def(
          "_load_all",
          [](M::Core::InferenceSession &session,
             AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<M::CompiledModels> &compiled,
             const nb::dict &weightsDict) {
            // Refcount-share — leaves the caller's Python AsyncValue
            // handle intact so the same compile result can be initialized
            // any number of times.
            return session.loadAll(compiled.copy(), weightsDict);
          },
          // No keep_alive needed: each returned ModelHandle holds an
          // nb::ref<InferenceSession> internally (see ModelHandle's
          // post-load constructor in InferenceSession.h).
          "compiled"_a, "weights_registry"_a)
      .def("compile",
           nb::overload_cast<std::filesystem::path,
                             std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&>(
               &M::Core::InferenceSession::compile),
           // The CompiledModels references framework context owned by the
           // session; keep the session alive while any AsyncValue is alive.
           nb::keep_alive<0, 1>(), "model_path"_a, "custom_extension_paths"_a,
           R"nbdoc(
      Compiles a model from a file path.

      Args:
          model_path: The path to the compiled model file (for example, a
              ``.mef`` file).
          custom_extension_paths: The paths to custom Mojo extension
              libraries.

      Returns:
          A handle to the compiled artifact, ready to be initialized with
          weights via ``_load_all``.
      )nbdoc")
      .def("compile",
           nb::overload_cast<const nb::capsule &,
                             std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&,
                             std::string &&, bool>(
               &M::Core::InferenceSession::compile),
           nb::keep_alive<0, 1>(), "model"_a, "custom_extensions"_a,
           "pipeline_name"_a, "tile_based_fusion"_a = false,
           R"nbdoc(
      Compiles a model from an in-memory capsule object.

      Args:
          model: A capsule containing the compiled model object.
          custom_extensions: The paths to custom Mojo extension libraries.
          pipeline_name: The name identifier for the compiled pipeline.
          tile_based_fusion: When ``True``, compiles the graph under the
              tile-based programming model. Defaults to ``False``.

      Returns:
          A handle to the compiled artifact, ready to be initialized with
          weights via ``_load_all``.
      )nbdoc")
      .def(
          "_wrap_compiled",
          [](M::Core::InferenceSession &self, M::CompiledModels &&models) {
            auto result = AsyncValueRef<M::CompiledModels>::allocate(
                self.getRuntimeContext().getCPUDevice());
            result.copy().emplace<M::CompiledModels>(std::move(models));
            return result;
          },
          nb::keep_alive<0, 1>(), "models"_a,
          R"nbdoc(
      Wraps an already-read ``CompiledModels`` in a resolved async handle.

      Consumes ``models``. The handle is allocated on this session's
      runtime and can be passed to :meth:`_load_all`.
      )nbdoc")
      .def(
          "set_debug_print_options",
          [](M::Core::InferenceSession &self, ResultOutputStyle style,
             unsigned int precision, const char *directory) {
            auto &ctx = self.getRuntimeContext().maxContext;
            DebugTensorPrintOptions &options =
                ctx->emplaceIfMissing<DebugTensorPrintOptions>();
            options.style = style;
            options.precision = precision;
            options.binaryDir = directory;
          },
          "style"_a, "precision"_a, "directory"_a,
          R"nbdoc(
      Sets debug output options for tensor printing during execution.

      Args:
          style: The output format style.
          precision: The number of decimal places for floating-point
              values.
          directory: The directory path for binary output files.
      )nbdoc")
      .def("set_mojo_define", &setMojoDefine<bool>, "key"_a, "value"_a,
           R"nbdoc(
      Sets a compile-time Mojo define to a boolean value.

      Args:
          key: The define name.
          value: The boolean value to assign.
      )nbdoc")
      .def("set_mojo_define", &setMojoDefine<int>, "key"_a, "value"_a,
           R"nbdoc(
      Sets a compile-time Mojo define to an integer value.

      Args:
          key: The define name.
          value: The integer value to assign.
      )nbdoc")
      .def("set_mojo_define", &setMojoDefine<const char *>, "key"_a, "value"_a,
           R"nbdoc(
      Sets a compile-time Mojo define to a string value.

      Args:
          key: The define name.
          value: The string value to assign.
      )nbdoc")
      .def_prop_ro("devices", &M::Core::InferenceSession::getDevices,
                   "The list of devices used by this session.")
      .def_prop_ro_static(
          "debug",
          [](nb::handle) -> M::Core::DebugConfig & {
            return M::Core::DebugConfig::instance();
          },
          nb::rv_policy::reference, "The unified debug configuration.");

  nb::enum_<ResultOutputStyle>(m, "PrintStyle", R"nbdoc(
      Controls the output format for debug tensor printing.

      Pass one of these values to :meth:`InferenceSession.set_debug_print_options`
      to configure how tensors are printed during execution.
  )nbdoc")
      .value("COMPACT", ResultOutputStyle::kCompact,
             "Compact human-readable format.")
      .value("FULL", ResultOutputStyle::kFull,
             "Full verbose format with all tensor details.")
      .value("BINARY", ResultOutputStyle::kBinary, "Raw binary format.")
      .value("BINARY_MAX_CHECKPOINT", ResultOutputStyle::kBinaryMaxCheckpoint,
             "Binary checkpoint format compatible with MAX.")
      .value("NONE", ResultOutputStyle::kNone, "Disables debug output.");

  M::Profiler::Python::addTracingToNanobindModuleClassMethods(
      m, "max._core.engine.");

  // https://nanobind.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ownership_adv.html#the-solution
  nb::intrusive_init(
      [](PyObject *o) noexcept {
        nb::gil_scoped_acquire guard;
        Py_INCREF(o);
      },
      [](PyObject *o) noexcept {
        nb::gil_scoped_acquire guard;
        Py_DECREF(o);
      });
}
