#ifndef SDK_ENGINEAPI_PYTHON_INFERENCESESSION_H
#define SDK_ENGINEAPI_PYTHON_INFERENCESESSION_H

#include "AsyncRT/Runtime/AsyncValueRef.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/Support/ModelTensorSpec.h"
#include "Kernels/max_license/WeightsRegistry.h"
#include "MLRT/Driver/DeviceContext/DeviceContext.h"
#include "_core/DLPack/Utils.h"
#include "_core/Driver/Buffer.h"
#include "_core/Driver/Device.h"
#include "max/max_license/API/c/CompiledModels.h"
#include "max/max_license/API/c/EngineConfig.h"
#include "max/max_license/API/c/EngineContext.h"
#include "nanobind/intrusive/counter.h"
#include "nanobind/intrusive/ref.h"
#include "nanobind/nanobind.h"
#include "llvm/ADT/STLExtras.h"
#include <memory>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

namespace nb = nanobind;

namespace M::Core {
class ModelHandle;

inline llvm::SmallVector<ModelTensorSpec>
getModelTensorSpecs(llvm::ArrayRef<std::string> names,
                    llvm::ArrayRef<QuantTensorSpec> specs) {
  return llvm::map_to_vector(llvm::zip_equal(names, specs),
                             [](const auto &pair) {
                               const auto &[name, spec] = pair;
                               return ModelTensorSpec{name, spec};
                             });
}

class InferenceSession final : public nb::intrusive_base {
public:
  InferenceSession(std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> &&devices,
                   std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&customExtensions,
                   size_t numThreads);

  AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels>
  compile(std::filesystem::path modelPath,
          std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&customExtensions);

  AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels>
  compile(const nb::capsule &model,
          std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&customExtensions,
          std::string &&pipelineName, bool tileBasedFusion);

  /// Initialize a single compiled model with the given weights, blocking until
  /// the model is ready. The \p model pointer must remain valid for the
  /// lifetime of the returned handle (i.e. the owning CompiledModels must
  /// outlive it).
  M::AsyncExecutableModel load(const M::Model *model,
                               WeightsRegistryRef weightsRegistry);

  /// Initializes all models in the compiled artifact and returns one
  /// ModelHandle per model in MEF order.
  ///
  /// Args:
  ///   compiledModels: The async compiled models to initialize.
  ///   weightsDict: A dictionary of weights used to initialize the models.
  ///
  /// Returns:
  ///   One ModelHandle per model encoded in the MEF, in MEF order.
  std::vector<ModelHandle> loadAll(AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
                                   const nb::dict &weightsDict);

  M::Engine::Context &getRuntimeContext() { return *runtimeContext; }

  /// Gets a list of devices that was initialized on the InferenceSession
  std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> getDevices() const { return devices; }

private:
  void
  addCustomExtensionToCompileConfig(CompilationRequest &compileConfig,
                                    std::filesystem::path custom_extension);
  CompilationRequest
  populateCompileConfig(std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&customExtensions);
  CompilationRequest sessionCompileConfig;
  M::Engine::Config runtimeConfig;
  std::unique_ptr<M::Engine::Context> runtimeContext;
  std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> devices;
};

/// A ModelHandle holds a reference to the internal (async) compiled model and
/// also a reference to the InferenceSession that was used to create the
/// ModelHandle. This is necessary because the ModelHandle delegates actual
/// loading to the InferenceSession so it is important for it to stay alive as
/// long as a ModelHandle is alive. Also, there can be multiple ModelHandle
/// instances per InferenceSession so a shared_ptr is appropriate. Refer to
/// this issue for a discussion on shared_ptr vs RCRef:
/// https://github.com/modularml/modular/issues/7706

/// We delegate loading to InferenceSession because it is the natural place to
/// store the runtimeContext which is necessary for model loading.
class ModelHandle {
public:
  /// Get a vector of all input tensors' specifications i.e. shape, dtype and
  /// name. Throws a std::invalid_argument if compiled models await fails.
  llvm::SmallVector<ModelTensorSpec> getInputMetadata();

  /// Get a vector of all output tensors' specifications i.e. shape and dtype.
  /// Throws a std::invalid_argument if compiled models await fails.
  llvm::SmallVector<ModelTensorSpec> getOutputMetadata();

  /// Get a vector of all devices setup by the InferenceSession attached to
  /// Model.
  std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> getDevices() const;

  /// Returns the async compiled models held by this handle, for passing to
  /// InferenceSession::loadAll.
  const AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> &getCompiledModels() const {
    return compiledModels;
  }

  /// Get the dSummary strings from all mgp.generic.execute primitives in the
  /// compiled model's execute function. Each summary describes the fused kernel
  /// composition (e.g. "Epilogue(custom__kv_rope, custom__kv_cache_store)").
  std::vector<std::string> getKernelSummaries();

  /// Get the symbol name of this model (the `sym_name` of its `mo.graph` op,
  /// preserved through MEF serialization). Used by the Python binding's
  /// `Model.name` property so callers of `InferenceSession.load_all` can key
  /// the returned dict by graph name instead of MEF position.
  std::string getName();

  /// Exports the compiled model as a mef to the filename passed.
  /// Args:
  ///   path: Name of the file where the mef is exported.
  void export_mef(const char *path);

  /// Reload weights into this compiled model in-place.
  ///
  /// Reuses the compiled graph and replaces the weight buffers in-place.
  ///
  /// Args:
  ///   weightsDict: A dictionary of weights used to reinitialize the model.
  void reload(const nb::dict &weightsDict);

  /// Drops the host-side weight references held by this handle.
  ///
  /// Releases the weights registry and the owning DLPack references, so the
  /// host weight memory can be freed once the caller drops its own
  /// references. Safe only when every weight was copied to its execution
  /// device during init: reading a host weight after this call is undefined
  /// behavior. `reload` remains usable afterwards.
  void releaseWeights();

  /// Runs inference with the boxed model.
  ///
  /// Args:
  ///   inputTensors: Inputs to be passed to the model.
  ///
  /// Returns:
  ///   List of outputs from the model
  std::vector<Driver::Python::Buffer>
  executeDeviceTensors(std::vector<Driver::Python::Buffer *> &inputTensors);

  /// Capture execution into a device graph collection using per-device keys.
  std::vector<Driver::Python::Buffer>
  capture(const std::vector<uint64_t> &graphKeys,
          std::vector<Driver::Python::Buffer *> &inputs);

  /// Replay the captured device graph collection for per-device keys.
  void replay(const std::vector<uint64_t> &graphKeys,
              std::vector<Driver::Python::Buffer *> &inputs);

  /// Execute eagerly and verify launch trace for per-device keys.
  void debugVerifyReplay(const std::vector<uint64_t> &graphKeys,
                         std::vector<Driver::Python::Buffer *> &inputs);

  /// Await all pending device graph instantiations.
  void awaitDeviceGraphs();

  /// Release captured device graphs for per-device keys, freeing the
  /// underlying device-side graph + working memory once the last reference
  /// drops. Releasing an unknown key is a no-op.
  void releaseCapturedGraphs(const std::vector<uint64_t> &graphKeys);

  // Devices of the model's input tensors.
  std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> inputDevicesPy;

  // Devices of the model's output tensors.
  std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> outputDevicesPy;

private:
  friend class InferenceSession;

  /// Construct a post-load handle for a single model within a compiled
  /// artifact. Used by InferenceSession::loadAll() to produce per-model
  /// handles.
  ModelHandle(AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
              nb::ref<InferenceSession> sessionPtr,
              M::AsyncExecutableModel loadedModel,
              WeightsRegistryRef weightsRegistry,
              std::shared_ptr<SmallVector<DLPack::DLManagedTensorWrapper>>
                  managedTensors,
              size_t modelIndex);

  /// Get a vector of all input tensors' device.
  /// Throws a std::invalid_argument if getting the device for any particular
  /// input is unsuccessful.
  std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> getInputDevices() const;

  /// Get a vector of all output tensors' device.
  /// Throws a std::invalid_argument if getting the device for any particular
  /// output is unsuccessful.
  std::vector<Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy> getOutputDevices() const;

  /// Internal API to allow for the execution of a model without tying it to how
  /// the inputs are prepared.
  std::vector<Driver::Python::Buffer>
  executePreparedDeviceTensors(M::Engine::Context &runtimeCtx,
                               SmallVectorImpl<AnyAsyncValueRef> &inputValues);

  /// Return the cpuDevice context of the associated InferenceSession.
  M::Engine::Context &getRuntimeContext() {
    return inferenceSession->getRuntimeContext();
  }

  // NOTE: inferenceSession must be declared before the models so that
  // inferenceSession is destroyed last.
  // This is because inferenceSession owns the AsyncRT::CPUDevice that the
  // models rely on to deallocate their buffers.
  nb::ref<InferenceSession> inferenceSession;
  AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels;
  M::AsyncExecutableModel loadedModel;
  // All handles from the same loadAll() call share this vector so that the
  // DLPack wrappers (and the numpy/torch arrays they pin) stay alive as long
  // as *any* handle from the batch is alive.  The weights registry holds raw
  // pointers into those arrays, so it must come after managedTensors in the
  // declaration (destroyed first) to keep the ordering safe.
  std::shared_ptr<SmallVector<DLPack::DLManagedTensorWrapper>> managedTensors;
  WeightsRegistryRef weightsRegistry;
  /// Index of this model within the compiled artifact's ModelList.
  size_t modelIndex;
};

} // namespace M::Core

#endif // SDK_ENGINEAPI_PYTHON_INFERENCESESSION_H

#include "max/max_license/API/c/EngineConfig.h"
#include "Support/Configuration.h"
#include "llvm/ADT/StringExtras.h"

using namespace M;
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// Config initialization
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// The runtime config initialization checks the modular.cfg file for a thread
// identifier to use, if specified, under the section 'triton_modular_backend'
// and key 'context_name'. If found, use it as the context name, otherwise
// use 'AsyncRT Thread ' as the prefix for threads in the thread pool.
M::Engine::Config::Config() {
  M::Config config;
  ErrorOr<M::Config> configOr = M::Config::open();
  if (!configOr.isError()) {
    config = std::move(*configOr);
  }

  // Extract a context name.
  llvm::StringRef val = config.getValue("runtime.context_name");
  if (!val.empty()) {
    contextThreadPoolName = val.str();
  }

  // Consider a default num_threads.
  val = config.getValue("runtime.num_threads");
  if (!val.empty()) {
    int parsedValue;
    if (llvm::to_integer<int>(val, parsedValue))
      setNumThreads(parsedValue);
  }

  // Extract a thread busy wait time.
  val = config.getValue("runtime.thread_busy_wait_time_us");
  if (!val.empty()) {
    size_t parsedValue;
    if (llvm::to_integer<size_t>(val, parsedValue))
      threadBusyWaitTime = std::chrono::microseconds(parsedValue);
  }
}

void M::Engine::Config::setNumThreads(size_t count) {
  numThreads = count; // May still be zero (intentional).
}

void M::Engine::Config::setMaxThreads(size_t count) {
  maxThreads = count; // May also be zero.
}

#ifndef GENERICML_API_COMPILEDMODELS_H
#define GENERICML_API_COMPILEDMODELS_H

#include "GraphCompiler/Driver/Common/DriverConfig.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/Driver/Common/DriverInputFormat.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/FrameworkFrontend.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MEFModel/MEFModel.h"
#include "MLRT/GraphRT/MEFExecutor/MEFFile.h"
#include "Support/Buffer.h"
#include "Support/DeviceSpecs.h"
#include "Support/ErrorOr.h"
#include "Support/ML/SizeUtils.h"
#include "Support/SymbolExport.h"
#include "max/max_license/API/c/EngineConfig.h"
#include "max/max_license/API/c/SourceModel.h"
#include "max/max_license/API/c/detail/ModelContext.h"
#include <filesystem>
#include <string>

namespace M {

/// Returns the preferred device
///   - the first accelerator in devices
///   - else the first CPU
///   — else nullptr if devices is empty
inline const M::Engine::ConfiguredDevice *
selectDevice(ArrayRef<M::Engine::ConfiguredDevice> devices) {
  for (const auto &device : devices)
    // Any non-CPU label counts as an accelerator
    if (device.spec->ref.label != kCPULabel)
      return &device;
  return devices.empty() ? nullptr : devices.data();
}

/// Returns the driver device config for `selectDevice(devices)`, or nullptr
/// if \p devices is empty.
inline std::unique_ptr<DriverConfig>
selectDeviceConfig(ArrayRef<M::Engine::ConfiguredDevice> devices) {
  const auto *device = selectDevice(devices);
  if (!device)
    return nullptr;
  const DeviceSpec &spec = *device->spec;
  return std::make_unique<DeviceConfig>(spec.ref.label, spec.ref.id, spec);
}

/// The internal type held by a `M_CompileConfig` that is created from
/// `M_newCompileConfig()`.
/// The `CompilationRequest` type represents the configs both for local and
/// CAS-aware compilation.
/// Note that this type can be used for a single compilation call. A new
/// `CompilationRequest` must be used for subsequent compilations.
class CompilationRequest {
public:
  CompilationRequest() = default;

  void addFrameworkConfig(std::unique_ptr<DriverConfig> config) {
    passthroughConfigs.push_back(std::move(config));
  }

  ArrayRef<std::unique_ptr<DriverConfig>> getFrameworkConfigs() const {
    return passthroughConfigs;
  }

  CompilationRequest(const CompilationRequest &other) {
    modelSource = other.modelSource;
    pipelineName = other.pipelineName;
    for (auto &config : other.passthroughConfigs)
      passthroughConfigs.push_back(config->clone());
  }

  CompilationRequest(CompilationRequest &&other) = default;
  CompilationRequest &operator=(CompilationRequest &&other) = default;

  CompilationRequest &operator=(const CompilationRequest &other) {
    modelSource = other.modelSource;
    pipelineName = other.pipelineName;
    for (auto &config : other.passthroughConfigs)
      passthroughConfigs.push_back(config->clone());
    return *this;
  }

  /// Get the underlying source model representation.
  std::optional<ModelSource> getModelSource() const {
    if (const ModelSource *val = std::get_if<ModelSource>(&modelSource))
      return *val;
    return std::nullopt;
  }

  /// Get the MAX Graph pipeline name.
  /// Only included if model source is a MAX Graph.
  std::optional<std::string> getPipelineName() const { return pipelineName; }

  /// Get the underlying path on the filesystem for where a model is.  This is
  /// used when compiling a model if the model ID is not set.
  std::optional<std::filesystem::path> getModelPath() const {
    if (const std::filesystem::path *path =
            std::get_if<std::filesystem::path>(&modelSource))
      return *path;
    return std::nullopt;
  }

  /// Set the underlying source model representation.
  void setModelSource(ModelSource source) {
    // Do not overwrite existing values.
    assert(std::holds_alternative<std::monostate>(modelSource));
    modelSource = source;
  }

  /// Sets the pipeline name if source is MAX Graph.
  void setPipelineName(std::string name) { pipelineName = name; }

  /// Sets the path for the model's CAS config.  This is set from the public
  /// API: `M_setModelPath`.
  void setModelPath(std::filesystem::path path) {
    // Do not overwrite existing values.
    assert(std::holds_alternative<std::monostate>(modelSource));
    modelSource = path;
  }

  /// Adds a path specifying the location of additional kernel libraries that
  /// should be loaded
  void addKernelLibraryPath(std::filesystem::path path) {
    passthroughConfigs.emplace_back(
        std::make_unique<KernelLibraryDriverConfig>(std::move(path)));
  }

  /// Enables (or disables) compiling the graph under the tile-based programming
  /// model. Set from the public API via the `tile_based_fusion` compile option.
  void setTileBasedFusion(bool tileBasedFusion) {
    // Remove any existing tile-based-fusion config so the latest value wins.
    llvm::erase_if(passthroughConfigs,
                   [](const std::unique_ptr<DriverConfig> &ptr) {
                     return isa<TileBasedFusionDriverConfig>(ptr.get());
                   });
    passthroughConfigs.emplace_back(
        std::make_unique<TileBasedFusionDriverConfig>(tileBasedFusion));
  }

  void setDevices(ArrayRef<M::Engine::ConfiguredDevice> devices) {
    // Remove any existing device config.
    llvm::erase_if(passthroughConfigs,
                   [](const std::unique_ptr<DriverConfig> &ptr) {
                     return isa<DeviceConfig>(ptr.get());
                   });

    if (auto deviceConfig = selectDeviceConfig(devices))
      passthroughConfigs.push_back(std::move(deviceConfig));
  }

private:
  std::vector<std::unique_ptr<DriverConfig>> passthroughConfigs;
  std::variant<std::monostate, std::filesystem::path, ModelSource> modelSource;
  std::optional<std::string> pipelineName;
};

/// `UninitializedModel` encapsulates the collection of `M::Model` instances
/// that are loaded from the compiled MEF but not yet initialized.
struct UninitializedModel {
  UninitializedModel(M::BufferRef buffer, ModelList models,
                     RCRef<MEFFile> handle)
      : compiledModelBuffer(std::move(buffer)), models(std::move(models)),
        mefHandle(std::move(handle)) {}

  UninitializedModel(UninitializedModel &&other) = default;
  UninitializedModel &operator=(UninitializedModel &&other) = default;

  size_t getNumModels() const { return models.size(); }
  const M::Model *getFirstModel() const {
    return models.empty() ? nullptr : models.front().get();
  }
  const M::Model *getModel(size_t i) const {
    return i < models.size() ? models[i].get() : nullptr;
  }

  ArrayRef<std::unique_ptr<const Model>> getModels() const { return models; }

  M::BufferRef getBuffer() { return compiledModelBuffer; }

private:
  UninitializedModel(const UninitializedModel &) = delete;
  void operator=(const UninitializedModel &) = delete;

  M::BufferRef compiledModelBuffer;
  ModelList models;
  RCRef<MEFFile> mefHandle;
};

/// The internal type created when compiling one or more models from the public
/// API: `M_compileModel`. `CompiledModels` contains information such as the
/// source model and all compiled models loaded to memory.
struct CompiledModels {

  CompiledModels(SourceModel sourceModel,
                 std::unique_ptr<MOFContext> frameworkCtx,
                 UninitializedModel uninitializedModel)
      : sourceModel(std::move(sourceModel)),
        frameworkCtx(std::move(frameworkCtx)),
        uninitializedModel(std::move(uninitializedModel)) {}

  CompiledModels(CompiledModels &&model) = default;

  /// Compiles a model from an opaque source representation with a known format.
  static ErrorOr<CompiledModels> create(M::ContextRef context,
                                        const CompilationRequest &compCfg,
                                        const M::Engine::Config &rtCfg);

  /// Reads previously compiled models from an in-memory MEF artifact.
  /// The buffer must satisfy `maxAttributeAlignment()` (file mappings
  /// always do).
  static MODULAR_CXX_EXPORT ErrorOr<CompiledModels> read(BufferRef buffer);

  const SourceModel &getSourceModel() const { return sourceModel; }
  size_t getNumModels() const { return uninitializedModel.getNumModels(); }
  const M::Model *getFirstModel() const {
    return uninitializedModel.getFirstModel();
  }
  const M::Model *getModel(size_t i) const {
    return uninitializedModel.getModel(i);
  }

  using iterator = ArrayRef<std::unique_ptr<const Model>>::iterator;

  /// Return the list references to each model.
  ArrayRef<std::unique_ptr<const Model>> getModels() const {
    return uninitializedModel.getModels();
  }

  /// Iterate over the list of models.
  iterator begin() const { return uninitializedModel.getModels().begin(); }
  iterator end() const { return uninitializedModel.getModels().end(); }

  M::BufferRef getBuffer() { return uninitializedModel.getBuffer(); }

private:
  static ErrorOr<CompiledModels> read(BufferRef buffer,
                                      std::unique_ptr<MOFContext> frameworkCtx,
                                      SourceModel sourceModel);

  SourceModel sourceModel;
  std::unique_ptr<MOFContext> frameworkCtx;
  UninitializedModel uninitializedModel;

  CompiledModels(const CompiledModels &other) = delete;
  void operator=(const CompiledModels &other) = delete;
};

} // namespace M

#endif // GENERICML_API_COMPILEDMODELS_H

#ifndef GENERICML_API_ENGINECONFIG_H
#define GENERICML_API_ENGINECONFIG_H

#include "MLRT/Driver/DeviceContext/DeviceContext.h"

namespace M::Engine {

/// A device the runtime may place work on: the MLRT context backing it, plus
/// the spec carrying the label and id the API surface exposes. The legacy
/// GenericML `Driver::Device` wrapper bundled exactly this pair (DRIV-399).
struct ConfiguredDevice {
  DeviceSpecRef spec;
  M::Driver::DeviceContextRef context;
};

/// Configuration object containing options applying to an
/// entire inference session.
class MODULAR_CXX_EXPORT Config {
public:
  Config();

  void setNumThreads(size_t count);

  size_t getNumThreads() const { return numThreads; }

  /// Internal only: this is used to limit the runtime.

  void setMaxThreads(size_t count);

  size_t getMaxThreads() const { return maxThreads; }

  /// Set the type of allocator used in the runtime. The values are
  /// defined in the enum M_AllocatorType.

  void setAllocatorType(int allocType) { this->allocatorType = allocType; }

  /// Get the type of allocator used in the runtime. The values are
  /// defined in the enum M_AllocatorType.

  int getAllocatorType() const { return allocatorType; }

  void addDevice(ConfiguredDevice device) {
    this->devices.push_back(std::move(device));
  }

  const std::vector<ConfiguredDevice> &getDevices() const {
    return this->devices;
  }

  // Set up API info.
  void setAPILanguage(const std::string &apiLanguage) {
    this->apiLanguage = apiLanguage;
  }

  StringRef getAPILanguage() const { return apiLanguage; }

  /// Get global context shared with Mojo.
  ContextRef getMaxContext() const { return maxContext; }

  /// Set global context shared with Mojo.
  void setMaxContext(M::Context *ctx) { maxContext = copyRCRef(ctx); }

  std::chrono::microseconds getThreadBusyWaitTime() const {
    return threadBusyWaitTime;
  }

  std::string_view getContextName() const { return contextThreadPoolName; }

  void enableCrashLog(const std::filesystem::path &path) {
    crashDumpDir = path;
    crashLogEnabled = true;
  }

  bool isCrashLogEnabled() const { return crashLogEnabled; }

  std::optional<std::filesystem::path> getCrashDumpDir() const {
    return crashDumpDir;
  }

private:
  size_t numThreads = 0;
  size_t maxThreads = 0;

  std::vector<ConfiguredDevice> devices;

  int allocatorType = 1; /* kCaching */
  std::string contextThreadPoolName = "🔥 Thread";
  std::chrono::microseconds threadBusyWaitTime = std::chrono::microseconds(200);
  std::optional<std::filesystem::path> crashDumpDir;
  bool crashLogEnabled = false;
  std::string apiLanguage = "c";
  ContextRef maxContext;
};

} // namespace M::Engine

#endif // GENERICML_API_ENGINECONFIG_H

// Backs Graph profile scope's _location() wrap loop: wraps `child` in a
// MOGG::ProfileScopeLocationAttr naming the active scope.
MlirLocation profile_scope_location(MlirContext ctx, const std::string &name,
                                    MlirLocation child,
                                    std::optional<std::string> color);

namespace nb = nanobind;
using namespace M::Graph;

// For named argument shorthand.
// See:
// https://nanobind.readthedocs.io/en/stable/basics.html#keyword-and-default-arguments
using namespace nanobind::literals;

namespace {
void load_modular_dialects(MlirDialectRegistry registry) {
  M::MO::loadDialects(*unwrap(registry));
}

MlirOperation next_operation(MlirOperation op) {
  mlir::Operation *x = unwrap(op);
  return wrap(x->getNextNode());
}

MlirOperation prev_operation(MlirOperation op) {
  mlir::Operation *x = unwrap(op);
  return wrap(x->getPrevNode());
}

MlirOperation last_operation(MlirBlock block) {
  mlir::Block *x = unwrap(block);

  if (x->empty())
    return wrap((mlir::Operation *)nullptr);
  return wrap(&x->back());
}

/// Initializes M::Context when no global context exists, then registers it on
/// the given MLIR context so loadContext() succeeds for graph compilation and
/// kernel analysis.
///
/// Reuses the existing global M::Context when present (e.g. after
/// InferenceSession) if Init::Options match; otherwise creates it via
/// Init::getOrCreateContext with cpuDevice options aligned with
/// Engine::Context::create's default session (see comments in-body).
static void _init_and_register_max_context(MlirContext mlirCtx) {
  M::Init::Options options;
  M::AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions rtOptions;
  // AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions defaults mainWillDonate to true; Engine's
  // getOrCreateCPUDeviceOptions forces false.
  rtOptions.mainWillDonate = false;
  options.withCPUDeviceOptions(rtOptions);
  // Engine::Config defaults isCrashLogEnabled() to false;
  // Engine::Context::create passes withForceDisableCrashReporting(!that).
  options.withForceDisableCrashReporting(true);

  auto ctxOr = M::Init::getOrCreateContext("max-graph", options);
  if (ctxOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(ctxOr.takeError().get());
  M::ContextRef maxContext = ctxOr.takeValue();

  M::registerContext(*unwrap(mlirCtx), maxContext);
}

M::ArrayElementsAttr array_attr(M::Driver::Python::Buffer &buffer,
                                M::MO::TensorType &type) {
  // Create an ND array from data, taking the size and shape from the tensor
  // type argument.
  auto spec = buffer.getSpec();

  llvm::ArrayRef<uint8_t> bytesArray(llvm::bit_cast<uint8_t *>(buffer.data()),
                                     spec.getSizeInBytes());

  auto dims = llvm::SmallVector<int64_t>(spec.begin(), spec.end());
  auto shapedType =
      mlir::RankedTensorType::get(type.getIntDims(), type.getElementType());

  return M::ArrayElementsAttr::get({bytesArray.data(), bytesArray.size()},
                                   shapedType);
}

char *frame_traceback(void *frame_ptr) {
  // This is simply
  // `''.join(traceback.format_list(frame))`
  nb::gil_scoped_acquire acquire{};
  auto frame = nb::handle(reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(frame_ptr));
  nb::object os = nb::module_::import_("traceback");
  nb::object formatStack = os.attr("format_list");
  auto empty = nb::str("");
  nb::object emptyJoin = empty.attr("join");

  auto outStr = nb::cast<std::string>(emptyJoin(formatStack(frame)));

  char *out = new char[outStr.size() + 1]{};
  // Copy to a string owned by the caller.
  outStr.copy(out, outStr.size());
  return out;
}

void frame_decref(void *frame_ptr) {
  // Destruction is always on the main thread controlled by python.
  // It will always have the gil.
  auto frame = nb::handle(reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(frame_ptr));
  frame.dec_ref();
}

void frame_incref(void *frame_ptr) {
  // Destruction is always on the main thread controlled by python.
  // It will always have the gil.
  auto frame = nb::handle(reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(frame_ptr));
  frame.inc_ref();
}

MlirLocation frame_loc(MlirContext ctx, nb::handle frame) {
  // The resulting location handles incrementing and decrementing the object's
  // reference count, as the object will be interned on the MLIR context.
  mlir::Location loc = M::RMO::PythonFrameAttr::getOpaque(
      unwrap(ctx), {.ptr = frame.ptr(),
                    .to_str = &frame_traceback,
                    .incref = &frame_incref,
                    .decref = &frame_decref});
  return wrap(loc);
}

// Serializes op and its descendants to MLIR bytecode with each op's
// Python-frame source location spelled out. The frames are attached as
// OpaqueLocs that hold a live callback and do not survive serialization, so
// they are materialized into serializable FusedLocs first. The materialization
// runs on a clone, so the caller's operation keeps its live OpaqueLocs.
//
// Bytecode rather than assembly text because this extension static-links its
// own LLVM: its textual float printer matches APFloat semantics by pointer
// against its own copy of the APFloatBase::sem* statics, so it mangles f64
// constants and aborts on any f32 that MLIR spells as a hex literal. Callers
// reparse this through max.mlir, which shares libmax's copy, and print there.
// See GEX-4052.
nb::bytes source_locations_bytecode(mlir::OpState &op) {
  mlir::OwningOpRef<mlir::Operation *> clone(op.getOperation()->clone());
  M::RMO::materializePythonFrameLocations(clone.get());
  std::string result;
  llvm::raw_string_ostream os(result);
  if (mlir::failed(mlir::writeBytecodeToFile(clone.get(), os)))
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "Failed to serialize operation with source locations to bytecode");
  return nb::bytes(result.data(), result.size());
}

/// Creates a Buffer directly from an MLIR constant attribute.
///
/// Supports:
/// - ArrayElementsAttr (#M.dense_array)
/// - AlignedBytesAttr (#M.aligned_bytes)
/// - DenseResourceElementsAttr (external blob)
///
/// Always copies data into a new buffer. Handles splatting when source
/// has 1 element but target shape requires more.
M::Driver::Python::Buffer
buffer_from_constant_attr(mlir::ElementsAttr attr, M::DType dtype,
                          const std::vector<size_t> &shape,
                          M::Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy device) {
  // Extract raw bytes based on attribute type
  llvm::ArrayRef<uint8_t> rawData;

  if (auto arrayAttr = llvm::dyn_cast<M::ArrayElementsAttr>(attr)) {
    rawData = arrayAttr.getRawData();
  } else if (auto alignedAttr = llvm::dyn_cast<M::AlignedBytesAttr>(attr)) {
    rawData = alignedAttr.getData();
  } else if (auto denseResource =
                 llvm::dyn_cast<mlir::DenseResourceElementsAttr>(attr)) {
    auto blob = denseResource.getRawHandle().getBlob();
    if (!blob)
      throw std::runtime_error("DenseResourceElementsAttr has no blob data");
    auto blobData = blob->getData();
    rawData = llvm::ArrayRef<uint8_t>(
        reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(blobData.data()), blobData.size());
  } else {
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "Unsupported constant attribute type for buffer creation");
  }

  // Calculate element counts
  size_t targetNumElements = 1;
  for (size_t dim : shape)
    targetNumElements *= dim;

  size_t elementSize = dtype.getSizeInBytes();
  size_t srcNumElements = rawData.size() / elementSize;

  // Validate for splatting
  if (srcNumElements != targetNumElements && srcNumElements != 1) {
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "Invalid constant: source has " + std::to_string(srcNumElements) +
        " elements but target has " + std::to_string(targetNumElements) +
        " elements (not a splat)");
  }

  // TODO(MXF-106): use Buffer.frombuffer when available.
  // Create buffer and copy data
  M::Driver::Python::Buffer buffer(dtype, shape, device);
  uint8_t *dstData = static_cast<uint8_t *>(buffer.data());

  if (srcNumElements == targetNumElements) {
    // Direct copy
    std::memcpy(dstData, rawData.data(), rawData.size());
  } else {
    // Splat: replicate single element
    for (size_t i = 0; i < targetNumElements; ++i) {
      std::memcpy(dstData + i * elementSize, rawData.data(), elementSize);
    }
  }

  return buffer;
}

} // namespace

void M::Graph::Python::bindGraphModule(nb::module_ m) {
  m.doc() = R"nbdoc(
        Provides Python bindings for the MAX Graph API.
    )nbdoc";

  /// Attribute factories

  /// Register dialects needed to build MAX graphs.
  m.def("load_modular_dialects", &load_modular_dialects,
        "Registers all Modular MLIR dialects into the given registry.");

  /// Creates an array attribute from any Python object that implements the
  /// buffer protocol.
  /// Copies the buffer data into the array attribute interned into the
  /// MLIRContext.
  m.def("array_attr", &array_attr,
        "Creates an array attribute from a buffer and tensor type.");

  /// Creates a Buffer from an MLIR constant attribute (inverse of array_attr).
  /// Copies data and handles splatting.
  m.def("_buffer_from_constant_attr", &buffer_from_constant_attr,
        nb::arg("attr"), nb::arg("dtype"), nb::arg("shape"), nb::arg("device"),
        "Creates a Buffer from an MLIR constant attribute.");

  m.def("next_operation", &next_operation,
        "Returns the next operation in the parent block, or ``None``.");
  m.def("prev_operation", &prev_operation,
        "Returns the previous operation in the parent block, or ``None``.");
  m.def("last_operation", &last_operation,
        "Returns the last operation in the given block, or ``None``.");

  /// Converts a dtype to an MLIR type.
  m.def("dtype_to_type",
        infer_context(+[](mlir::MLIRContext *ctx, M::DType dtype) {
          auto mlirType = M::MO::toMLIRType(ctx, dtype);
          if (mlirType.isError())
            throw std::runtime_error("Invalid dtype");
          return *mlirType;
        }),
        "Converts a MAX :class:`DType` to the corresponding MLIR type.");

  m.def(
      "type_to_dtype",
      [](mlir::Type dtype) -> M::DType {
        ErrorOr<DType> type = M::MO::fromMLIRType(dtype);
        if (type.isError())
          throw std::runtime_error("Invalid type");
        return *type;
      },
      "Converts an MLIR type to the corresponding MAX :class:`DType`.");

  /// Creates an opaque location containing a python frame.
  m.def("frame_loc", &frame_loc,
        "Creates an opaque MLIR location containing a Python stack frame.");

  m.def("profile_scope_location", &profile_scope_location, "ctx"_a, "name"_a,
        "child"_a, "color"_a = std::nullopt,
        "Wraps `child` in a MOGG::ProfileScopeLocationAttr naming the active "
        "Graph.profile_scope(), with an optional color.");

  /// Serializes an operation to MLIR bytecode with Python source locations
  /// materialized, so a graph dumped without compiling it still shows where
  /// each op was built. Does not mutate the operation.
  m.def("source_locations_bytecode", &source_locations_bytecode, "op"_a,
        "Serializes the operation to MLIR bytecode with each op's Python "
        "source location materialized into printable form. Print it by "
        "reparsing through max.mlir. Does not mutate the operation.");

  m.def("_init_and_register_max_context", &_init_and_register_max_context,
        "mlir_ctx"_a,
        R"nbdoc(
      Initializes a process-wide M::Context when none exists, then registers it with the given MLIR context so compiler code can use loadContext.

      Internal API; does not expose M::Context to Python. New contexts are
      created via Init::getOrCreateContext (same Init path the Engine uses before
      attaching devices).
  )nbdoc");

  //===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
  // KernelLibrary (backed by `mogg.kernel.decl` / `mogg.primitive.decl` ops)
  //===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

  nb::class_<Python::KernelTorchInfo>(m, "KernelTorchInfo", R"nbdoc(
      The info needed to register a Mojo kernel as a PyTorch custom op.

      Built by :obj:`max.experimental.torch` from the kernel's ``execute``
      signature via ``KernelDeclAdaptor``.
  )nbdoc")
      .def_ro("num_dps_outputs", &Python::KernelTorchInfo::numDpsOutputs,
              "The number of leading destination-passing-style output "
              "arguments.")
      .def_ro("tensor_arg_names", &Python::KernelTorchInfo::tensorArgNames,
              "The source names of tensor-like arguments in declaration "
              "order (DPS outputs first, then inputs).");

  nb::class_<Python::Analysis>(m, "Analysis", R"nbdoc(
      Analyzes Mojo kernel libraries for custom operator integration.

      Loads one or more Mojo shared libraries and exposes their exported
      kernel operations for use in MAX graphs. Used internally to validate
      and register custom operations.

      Args:
          context: A Mojo library object or path.
          paths: The additional library search paths.
  )nbdoc")
      .def(nb::init<nb::object, std::vector<std::filesystem::path>>(),
           "context"_a, "paths"_a)
      .def_prop_ro("symbol_names", &Analysis::symbolNames,
                   "The list of exported kernel symbol names.")
      .def_prop_ro("library_paths", &Analysis::libraryPaths,
                   "The paths of all loaded libraries.")
      .def(
          "kernel",
          [](Analysis *self, const std::string &name) {
            return M::Graph::Python::castOp(self->kernelOp(name));
          },
          "Returns the MLIR operation for the named kernel symbol.")
      .def("verify_custom_op", &Analysis::verifyCustomOp,
           "Verifies that an operation matches the expected kernel signature.")
      .def("add_path", &Analysis::addPath,
           "Adds a library search path to this analysis.")
      .def("seed_kernel_decls", &Analysis::seedKernelDecls,
           "Copies kernel decl ops and the opaque-type mapping attribute "
           "into the given target module. Called by the compile path to "
           "seed a model module so the GC pipeline can skip "
           "``mogg-import-packages``.")
      .def("kernel_torch_info", &Analysis::kernelTorchInfo, "name"_a,
           "Returns the :class:`KernelTorchInfo` that "
           ":obj:`max.experimental.torch` needs to register the named kernel "
           "as a PyTorch custom op. Raises ``ValueError`` if the kernel is "
           "unknown or has an unsupported argument type.")
      .def("has_shape_function", &Analysis::hasShapeFunction, "name"_a,
           "Returns true if a shape function is registered for the named "
           "kernel.");

  M::Profiler::Python::addTracingToNanobindModuleClassMethods(
      m, "max._core.graph.");
}

MlirLocation profile_scope_location(MlirContext ctx, const std::string &name,
                                    MlirLocation child,
                                    std::optional<std::string> color) {
  mlir::MLIRContext *ctxPtr = unwrap(ctx);
  mlir::StringAttr colorAttr =
      color ? mlir::StringAttr::get(ctxPtr, *color) : mlir::StringAttr();
  mlir::Location loc = M::MOGG::ProfileScopeLocationAttr::get(
      ctxPtr, mlir::StringAttr::get(ctxPtr, name), unwrap(child), colorAttr);
  return wrap(loc);
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// RuntimeContext initialization
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

static CPUDeviceOptions
getOrCreateCPUDeviceOptions(const Engine::Config &config,
                            StringRef profileFilename) {
  AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions cpuDeviceOptions;
  cpuDeviceOptions.numThreads = config.getNumThreads();
  cpuDeviceOptions.maxThreads = config.getMaxThreads();
  cpuDeviceOptions.tcmallocAllocator =
      config.getAllocatorType() == (int)kCaching;
  cpuDeviceOptions.threadBusyWaitTime = config.getThreadBusyWaitTime().count();
  cpuDeviceOptions.profileFilename = profileFilename;
  cpuDeviceOptions.poolName = config.getContextName();
  if (cpuDeviceOptions.numThreads == 1)
    cpuDeviceOptions.withSingleThreaded();
  // Previously mainWillDonate was required to be false in order to avoid the
  // Runtime created by the Engine from overwriting the Runtime created by the
  // Mojo stdlib during startup, this is no longer the case. Though there is
  // still a question of whether the Engine should be initialized with
  // mainWillDonate as true or false, setting to true currently causes an issue
  // with integration with the Torch inductor. See GEX-3387 for details.
  cpuDeviceOptions.mainWillDonate = false;

  return cpuDeviceOptions;
}

static void setUnknownLocError(AnyAsyncValueRef &&asyncVal, Error error) {
  std::move(asyncVal).setToError(
      {std::move(error), UnknownLocationDecoder::getEncodedLocation()});
}

static ErrorOr<std::unique_ptr<ExecutableModel>>
createExecutableModel(const M::Model *model, CPUDevice &cpuDevice,
                      const Engine::Config &config,
                      const WeightsRegistry *weightsRegistry) {
  M::GraphCompiler::Driver::DeviceMap deviceMap;
  for (const auto &device : config.getDevices())
    deviceMap.insert({device.spec->ref, device.context});
  auto executableModelOr = model->setup(cpuDevice, weightsRegistry, deviceMap);
  if (executableModelOr.isError())
    return executableModelOr.takeError().getMessage().copy();

  auto executableModel = executableModelOr.takeValue();
  auto setupErrorOrSuccess = executableModel->waitForModelSetup();
  if (setupErrorOrSuccess.isError())
    return Error(Twine("Model setup failed, not ready for execution.  "
                       "Modular internal detail: ") +
                 setupErrorOrSuccess.getError());
  return std::move(executableModel);
}

static ErrorOr<ExecutableModels>
createExecutableModels(const CompiledModels &compiledModels,
                       CPUDevice &cpuDevice, const Engine::Config &config,
                       const WeightsRegistry *weightsRegistry) {
  if (compiledModels.getNumModels() == 0)
    return Error::getStaticString(
        "Compiled model does not contain any valid models");

  ExecutableModels results;
  results.reserve(compiledModels.getNumModels());

  for (const std::unique_ptr<const Model> &model : compiledModels) {
    ErrorOr<std::unique_ptr<ExecutableModel>> executableModelOr =
        createExecutableModel(model.get(), cpuDevice, config, weightsRegistry);
    if (executableModelOr.isError())
      return executableModelOr.takeError();
    results.push_back(executableModelOr.takeValue());
  }
  return results;
}

static ErrorOr<TensorMap>
executeExecutableModel(const ExecutableModel &executableModel,
                       TensorMap &inputMap, CPUDevice &cpuDevice) {
  auto inputNames = executableModel.getModel()->getInputNames();

  SmallVector<AnyAsyncValueRef> inputValuesInMEFIndexOrder;
  inputValuesInMEFIndexOrder.reserve(inputMap.tensors.size());

  // Iterating on names in MEF order here.
  for (auto inputName : inputNames) {
    auto it = inputMap.tensors.find(inputName);
    if (it == inputMap.tensors.end()) {
      return Error("The model requires an input tensor named '" + inputName +
                   "' but it was not provided.");
    }

    inputValuesInMEFIndexOrder.emplace_back(it->second.copy());
  }

  auto results = executableModel.execute(inputValuesInMEFIndexOrder);

  if (results.empty())
    return Error("Failed to execute model");

  if (auto err = AsyncRT::awaitOrError(results))
    return err.takeError();

  MutableArrayRef<AnyAsyncValueRef> resultCopy(results.data(), results.size());
  resultCopy = resultCopy.drop_front();
  llvm::SmallVector<AnyAsyncValueRef> outputTensorRefs;
  outputTensorRefs.reserve(resultCopy.size());
  for (auto &result : resultCopy) {
    outputTensorRefs.push_back(std::move(result));
  }

  AsyncRT::await(outputTensorRefs);

  llvm::StringMap<AnyAsyncValueRef> resultMap;
  auto outputNames = executableModel.getModel()->getOutputNames();
  for (auto [outIdx, tensor] : llvm::enumerate(outputTensorRefs)) {
    if (tensor.isError())
      return tensor.getDiagnostic().getMessage().copy();

    resultMap.insert({outputNames[outIdx], std::move(tensor)});
  }

  return TensorMap(std::move(resultMap), cpuDevice);
}

ErrorOr<Engine::Context>
Engine::Context::create(const M::Engine::Config &config) {
  std::string profileFilename =
      llvm::sys::Process::GetEnv("MODULAR_PROFILE_FILENAME").value_or("");

  ContextRef maxContext;
  if (ContextRef ctx = config.getMaxContext()) {
    maxContext = std::move(ctx);
  } else {
    Init::Options options;
    CPUDeviceOptions rtOptions =
        getOrCreateCPUDeviceOptions(config, profileFilename);
    options.withCPUDeviceOptions(rtOptions);
    options.withForceDisableCrashReporting(!config.isCrashLogEnabled());

    auto contextOr = Init::getOrCreateContext("max-engine", options);
    if (contextOr.isError())
      return contextOr.takeError();
    maxContext = contextOr.takeValue();
  }
  auto runtimeContext = Engine::Context(config, maxContext.copy());
  auto &maxTelemetryContext =
      runtimeContext.maxContext
          ->emplaceIfMissing<GML::MaxEngineTelemetryContext>(maxContext.copy());
  maxTelemetryContext.setAPILanguage(config.getAPILanguage().str());

  // Source of truth for the closed set of valid device labels. Downstream
  // consumers (notably the C-API M_HOST vs M_ACCELERATOR predicate in
  // M_getDeviceType / M_getDeviceTypeFromSpec) treat anything not rejected
  // here as a valid device, so this guard must stay in sync with the
  // kCPULabel / kGPULabel constants in Support/DeviceSpecs.h.
  for (const auto &device : config.getDevices()) {
    const DeviceSpec &spec = *device.spec;
    if (spec.ref.label != kCPULabel && spec.ref.label != kGPULabel) {
      return Error(Twine("unrecognized device '") + spec.ref.label + "'");
    }
    // else: no special extra device handling
  }
  return runtimeContext;
}

Engine::Context::Context(Context &&other)
    : maxContext(std::move(other.maxContext)), config(std::move(other.config)),
      cpuDevice(*maxContext->get<CPUDevice>()) {}

Engine::Context::Context(const M::Engine::Config &runtimeConfig,
                         M::ContextRef context)
    : maxContext(std::move(context)), config(runtimeConfig),
      cpuDevice(*maxContext->get<CPUDevice>()) {
  crashRecoveryContext.DumpStackAndCleanupOnFailure = true;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// Model compilation, loading, and initialization
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels>
Engine::Context::compileModel(CompilationRequest config) const {
  auto compiledModelAsync = AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels>::allocate(cpuDevice);

  addTask(cpuDevice, [config = std::move(config),
                      compiledModelAsync = compiledModelAsync.copy(),
                      this]() mutable {
    auto compiledModelOr = compileModelSync(std::move(config));

    auto &telemetryCtx = *maxContext->get<GML::MaxEngineTelemetryContext>();

    if (compiledModelOr.isError()) {
      Error compileError = compiledModelOr.takeError();
      // FIXME: This potentially can contain absolute file paths in user
      // machine. We might need to scrub that.
      Telemetry::emitCompileInfo("compile.failure", telemetryCtx,
                                 compileError.copy());
      return setUnknownLocError(std::move(compiledModelAsync),
                                std::move(compileError));
    }

    Telemetry::emitCompileInfo("compile.success", telemetryCtx, {});
    std::move(compiledModelAsync).emplace(compiledModelOr.takeValue());
  });

  return compiledModelAsync;
}

static void telemetryEmitModelFormat(FileFormat format, ContextRef context) {
  auto telemetryContext = context->get<Telemetry::TelemetryContext>();
  Telemetry::emitCompiledModelType(*telemetryContext, format);
}

static void telemetryEmitPipelineName(std::string_view pipelineName,
                                      ContextRef context) {
  auto telemetryContext = context->get<Telemetry::TelemetryContext>();
  Telemetry::emitPipelineName("max.pipeline.run", *telemetryContext,
                              pipelineName);
}

/// Compiles a model. Functionally identical to `M_compileModel`, but blocks
/// on execution. Unlike `M_compileModel`, the user does not need to call
/// `M_waitForCompilation` to await a compilation result. Also does not use CAS
/// for kernel caching.
ErrorOr<CompiledModels>
Engine::Context::compileModelSync(CompilationRequest config) const {
  config.setDevices(this->config.getDevices());
  auto modelOr =
      CompiledModels::create(maxContext.copy(), config, this->config);
  if (modelOr.isError())
    return modelOr.takeError();

  if (auto pipelineName = config.getPipelineName(); pipelineName)
    telemetryEmitPipelineName(*pipelineName, maxContext);
  telemetryEmitModelFormat(modelOr.get().getSourceModel().format(), maxContext);

  return modelOr.takeValue();
}

ErrorOrSuccess Engine::Context::await(AnyAsyncValueRef value) {
  return AsyncRT::awaitOrError(value);
}

M::AsyncExecutableModel
Engine::Context::initModel(const M::Model *model,
                           const WeightsRegistryRef &weightsRegistry) const {
  using ModelType = std::unique_ptr<M::ExecutableModel>;
  auto result = AsyncValueRef<ModelType>::allocate(cpuDevice);

  // Run on a cpuDevice worker thread to ensure AsyncRT cpuDevice is set in TLS.
  // (MGP_RT_BufferBorrowV2, called during Model::setup, requires a valid
  // current cpuDevice.)
  addTask(cpuDevice, [model, weights = weightsRegistry.copy(),
                      result = result.copy(), this]() mutable {
    auto executableModelOr = createExecutableModel(
        model, cpuDevice, getConfig(), weights.getPointer());
    if (executableModelOr.isError())
      return setUnknownLocError(std::move(result),
                                executableModelOr.takeError());
    std::move(result).emplace(executableModelOr.takeValue());
  });

  return result;
}

AsyncValueRef<ExecutableModels>
Engine::Context::initModel(AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
                           const WeightsRegistryRef &weightsRegistry) const {
  auto result = AsyncValueRef<ExecutableModels>::allocate(cpuDevice);

  // Use andThenAsync to ensure createExecutableModels runs on a cpuDevice
  // worker thread.  The caller may be a foreign thread (e.g. a Python
  // ThreadPoolExecutor thread) that has no AsyncRT cpuDevice set in its
  // thread-local storage; MGP_RT_BufferBorrowV2 (called during Model::setup)
  // requires a valid current cpuDevice.
  std::move(compiledModels)
      .andThenAsync(
          [result = result.copy(), weights = weightsRegistry.copy(),
           this](AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> &&compiledModelsRef) mutable {
            if (compiledModelsRef.isError())
              return setUnknownLocError(
                  std::move(result),
                  compiledModelsRef.takeDiagnostic().getMessage().copy());

            auto executableModelsOr =
                createExecutableModels(compiledModelsRef.get(), cpuDevice,
                                       getConfig(), weights.getPointer());
            if (executableModelsOr.isError())
              return setUnknownLocError(std::move(result),
                                        executableModelsOr.takeError());

            std::move(result).emplace(executableModelsOr.takeValue());
          });

  return result;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// Model execution
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

AsyncValueRef<TensorMap>
Engine::Context::execute(AsyncExecutableModel executableModel,
                         AsyncValueRef<TensorMap> inputTensorMap) const {
  auto outputTensorMap = AsyncValueRef<TensorMap>::allocate(cpuDevice);
  AsyncExecutableModel executableModelRef = executableModel.copy();
  executableModel.andThenAsync([this, inTensorMap = inputTensorMap.copy(),
                                outTensorMap = outputTensorMap.copy(),
                                executableModelRef =
                                    std::move(executableModelRef)]() mutable {
    if (executableModelRef.isError()) {
      return std::move(outTensorMap)
          .setToError(executableModelRef.takeDiagnostic());
    }

    AsyncRT::await(inTensorMap);
    auto &inputMap = inTensorMap.get();

    std::unique_ptr<ExecutableModel> &executableModel =
        executableModelRef.get();
    if (!executableModel) {
      return std::move(outTensorMap)
          .setToError({Error::getStaticString("Executable model not available"),
                       UnknownLocationDecoder::getEncodedLocation()});
    }

    ErrorOr<TensorMap> outputsOr =
        executeExecutableModel(*executableModel, inputMap, cpuDevice);
    if (outputsOr.isError()) {
      const Model *model = executableModel->getModel();
      return std::move(outTensorMap)
          .setToError({outputsOr.takeError(),
                       model ? model->getLocation().copy()
                             : UnknownLocationDecoder::getEncodedLocation()});
    }
    std::move(outTensorMap).emplace(outputsOr.takeValue());
  });
  return outputTensorMap;
}

ErrorOr<ArrayRef<QuantTensorSpec>>
Engine::Context::getInputSpecs(AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
                               size_t modelIndex) {
  if (auto err = AsyncRT::awaitOrError(compiledModels))
    return err.takeError();

  if (auto model = compiledModels->getModel(modelIndex))
    return model->getInputSpecs();

  return Error::getStaticString("model index out of bounds");
}

ErrorOr<ArrayRef<QuantTensorSpec>>
Engine::Context::getOutputSpecs(AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
                                size_t modelIndex) {
  if (auto err = AsyncRT::awaitOrError(compiledModels))
    return err.takeError();

  if (auto model = compiledModels->getModel(modelIndex))
    return model->getOutputSpecs();

  return Error::getStaticString("model index out of bounds");
}

ErrorOr<ArrayRef<std::string>>
Engine::Context::getInputNames(AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
                               size_t modelIndex) {
  if (auto err = AsyncRT::awaitOrError(compiledModels))
    return err.takeError();

  if (auto model = compiledModels->getModel(modelIndex))
    return model->getInputNames();

  return Error::getStaticString("model index out of bounds");
}

ErrorOr<ArrayRef<std::string>>
Engine::Context::getOutputNames(AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
                                size_t modelIndex) {
  if (auto err = AsyncRT::awaitOrError(compiledModels))
    return err.takeError();

  if (auto model = compiledModels->getModel(modelIndex))
    return model->getOutputNames();

  return Error::getStaticString("model index out of bounds");
}

ErrorOr<std::vector<std::string>> Engine::Context::getKernelSummaries(
    const AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> &compiledModels, size_t modelIndex) {
  if (auto err = AsyncRT::awaitOrError(compiledModels))
    return err.takeError();

  if (auto model = compiledModels->getModel(modelIndex))
    return model->getKernelSummaries();

  return Error::getStaticString("model index out of bounds");
}

ErrorOr<Engine::ConfiguredDevice>
Engine::Context::resolveDevice(M::DeviceRef deviceRef) const {
  for (auto &device : getConfig().getDevices())
    if (deviceRef == device.spec->ref)
      return device;
  return Error(Twine("unrecognized device '") + deviceRef.toString() + "'");
}

#include "Init/Init.h"
#include "AsyncRT/Runtime/HostSystem.h"
#include "Init/DevelopmentSignalHandler.h"
#include "Support/Configuration.h"
#include "Support/ContextGlobal.h"
#include "Support/CrashReporting/CrashReporting.h"
#include "Support/Telemetry/Telemetry.h"

#include "llvm/Support/ErrorHandling.h"
#include "llvm/Support/Process.h"

#include <mutex>

using namespace M;

static constexpr bool isProductionBuild() {
#ifdef MODULAR_PRODUCTION
  return true;
#else
  return false;
#endif
}

namespace {

/// Internal function for creating an M::Context, not thread-safe, and not
/// intended for use outside of this file.
ErrorOr<ContextRef> createContextImpl(StringRef programName,
                                      const Init::Options &options,
                                      StringRef subCommand) {
  // Create the top-level context.
  ContextRef ctx = ContextRef::create();

  // Create the settings object.
  auto settingsOr = Config::open();
  if (settingsOr.isError())
    return settingsOr.takeError();
  Config settings = std::move(*settingsOr);

  bool crashReportingEnabled = Telemetry::isCrashReportingEnabled(settings);

  // Enable crash logging, if appropriate.
  if (!isProductionBuild() && !crashReportingEnabled)
    Init::registerDevelopmentSignalHandler(programName);
  else if (!options.forceDisableCrashReportingEnabled() &&
           crashReportingEnabled) {
    // The crash lane must carry the same machine/session IDs as the usage
    // telemetry lane so crash reports can be joined with usage events.
    const auto &localIDs = Telemetry::createLocalIDs();
    initCrashpadForProgram(programName, localIDs.machine,
                           localIDs.machineSource, localIDs.session, &settings);
  }

  // TelemetryContext created and added to the Context here as Config is
  // required.
  ctx->emplace<Telemetry::TelemetryContext>(settings, programName, subCommand);

  // Create a new cpuDevice (if needed).
  if (options.getCPUDeviceOptions()) {
    std::string profileFilename =
        llvm::sys::Process::GetEnv("MODULAR_PROFILE_FILENAME").value_or("");
    AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions opts = *options.getCPUDeviceOptions();
    if (!profileFilename.empty())
      opts.profileFilename = profileFilename;
    AsyncRT::CPUDeviceRef ref = AsyncRT::getOrCreateCPUDevice(
        AsyncRT::CPUDeviceSource::MaxContext, opts);
    ctx->setRuntime(GenericRCRef::fromRCRef(std::move(ref)));
  }

  // Finally move the settings.
  ctx->emplace<Config>(std::move(settings));

  // Store a copy of the init options so we can compare when reusing the
  // global context.
  ctx->emplace<Init::Options>(options);

  // Return the useable context.
  return std::move(ctx);
}

} // namespace

ErrorOr<ContextRef> Init::createContext(StringRef programName,
                                        const Init::Options &options,
                                        StringRef subCommand) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getGlobalContextMutex());
  if (getCurrentMaxContextPointerOrNull()) {
    llvm::report_fatal_error(
        "Init::createContext() attempted to create a new M::Context when one"
        "already exists, considering using Init::getContext() instead.");
  }

  // Create context.
  auto ctxOr = createContextImpl(programName, options, subCommand);
  if (ctxOr.isError())
    return ctxOr.takeError();

  // Set as the global current context.
  setCurrentMaxContextPointer(ctxOr->getPointer());
  return ctxOr;
}

ErrorOr<ContextRef> Init::getOrCreateContext(StringRef programName,
                                             const Init::Options &options,
                                             StringRef subCommand) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getGlobalContextMutex());
  if (Context *existing = getCurrentMaxContextPointerOrNull()) {
    if (*existing->get<Init::Options>() != options)
      llvm::report_fatal_error(
          "Init::getOrCreateContext() requested an M::Context with different"
          "Init::Options to those used to create the existing M::Context, check"
          "the options that are being requested.");
    return ContextRef::copy(existing);
  }

  // Create context.
  auto ctxOr = createContextImpl(programName, options, subCommand);
  if (ctxOr.isError())
    return ctxOr.takeError();

  // Set as the global current context.
  setCurrentMaxContextPointer(ctxOr->getPointer());
  return ctxOr;
}

ContextRef Init::getContext() {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getGlobalContextMutex());
  Context *existing = getCurrentMaxContextPointerOrNull();
  if (!existing) {
    llvm::report_fatal_error(
        "Init::getContext() requested the M::Context but no context has been"
        "created yet, Init::createContext() must be called to create the"
        "M::Context before calling Init::getContext().");
  }

  return ContextRef::copy(existing);
}

#ifndef SUPPORT_CONTEXT_H
#define SUPPORT_CONTEXT_H

#include "Support/ADT/GenericRCRef.h"
#include "Support/ADT/GenericUniquePtrSet.h"
#include "Support/ErrorOr.h"
#include "Support/RCRef.h"
#include "Support/ReferenceCounted.h"
#include "Support/SymbolExport.h"
#include "Support/TypeID.h"
#include "llvm/ADT/FunctionExtras.h"
#include <memory>

namespace M {

class Context : public ReferenceCounted<Context> {
public:
  /// Transfers ptr into the context object set.
  template <typename T>
  void set(std::unique_ptr<T> ptr) {
    storage.set(std::move(ptr));
  }

  /// Sets the cpuDevice for this context, called at context creation. Uses
  /// GenericRCRef because of a circular dependency (Context -> AsyncRT/Runtime
  /// -> AsyncRT/Support -> MArchTarget -> MDialect -> Context). See GEX-3400.
  void setRuntime(GenericRCRef ref) { cpuDeviceRef = std::move(ref); }

  /// Emplaces a new object of type T into the context object set and returns a
  /// reference to it.
  template <typename T, typename... Args>
  T &emplace(Args &&...args) {
    return storage.emplace<T, Args...>(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Returns a reference to the object of type T held by the context object
  /// set. If it does not contain such an object, emplaces a new object and
  /// returns a reference to it.
  template <typename T, typename... Args>
  T &emplaceIfMissing(Args &&...args) {
    return storage.emplaceIfMissing<T, Args...>(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Returns a pointer to the object of type T held by the context object set.
  /// If it does not contain such an object, calls the creator function to
  /// create one and install. Returns any error the creator function returns.
  template <typename T>
  ErrorOr<T *> createIfMissing(
      llvm::unique_function<ErrorOr<std::unique_ptr<T>>()> creator) {
    return storage.createIfMissing<T>(std::move(creator));
  }

  /// Returns a pointer to the context object of type T held by the context
  /// object set, or nullptr if no such object exists. The CPUDeviceRef is
  /// stored as a separate member so is checked first.
  template <typename T>
  T *get() {
    if (cpuDeviceRef && cpuDeviceRef.getTypeID() == TypeID::get<T>())
      return cpuDeviceRef.get<T>();
    return storage.get<T>();
  }

  MODULAR_CXX_EXPORT ~Context();

private:
  GenericRCRef cpuDeviceRef;
  GenericUniquePtrSet storage;
};

/// Convenience definitions.
using ContextRef = RCRef<Context>;

} // namespace M

#endif // SUPPORT_CONTEXT_H

#include "AsyncRT/Runtime/HostSystem.h"
#include "AsyncRT/Runtime/Globals/RuntimeGlobal.h"
#include "Support/Threading/HWInfo.h"

#include "llvm/Support/ErrorHandling.h"

#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>

namespace M::AsyncRT {

CPUDeviceRef getOrCreateCPUDevice(CPUDeviceSource source,
                                  const CPUDeviceOptions &options,
                                  bool allowUsingExistingOptions) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(getGlobalCPUDeviceMutex());
  CPUDevice *existingCPUDevice = getGlobalCPUDevicePointer();
  if (existingCPUDevice) {
    if (getStoredGlobalCPUDeviceCreationOptions() != options &&
        !allowUsingExistingOptions)
      llvm::report_fatal_error("AsyncRT::getOrCreateCPUDevice called "
                               "requesting different options to "
                               "those used to create the existing CPUDevice.");
    return CPUDeviceRef::copy(existingCPUDevice);
  }

  assert(CPUDevice::getCurrentCPUDeviceOrNull() == nullptr &&
         "creating a CPUDevice from a thread already associated with an outer "
         "CPUDevice");
  CompactCPUDevicePtr cpuDevicePtr = CompactCPUDevicePtr::reserve();
  std::unique_ptr<Allocator> allocator =
      getAllocator(options.getAllocatorOptions());
  std::unique_ptr<WorkQueue> workQueue;
  std::map<int, CPUDevice *> numaDevices;
  CPUDeviceType topLevelType = CPUDeviceType::kGlobal;
  switch (options.workQueueType) {
  case CPUDeviceOptions::WorkQueueType::kSingleThread:
    workQueue = createSingleThreadWorkQueue(cpuDevicePtr);
    break;
  case CPUDeviceOptions::WorkQueueType::kThreadPool:
    if (options.numaPartitioned) {
      // For each NUMA node, create a separate CPUDevice with its own
      // CompactCPUDevicePtr and partitioned ThreadPoolWorkQueue. The top-level
      // CPUDevice owns these NUMA node partitioned devices; its
      // DelegateThreadPoolWorkQueue has pointers to the delegate
      // ThreadPoolWorkQueues.
      const ErrorOr<NUMATopology> &topologyOr = NUMATopology::get();
      if (topologyOr.isError())
        llvm::report_fatal_error(topologyOr.getError());
      const std::vector<int> &numaNodes = topologyOr->getNumaNodes();
      std::vector<WorkQueue *> delegateWorkQueues;
      delegateWorkQueues.reserve(numaNodes.size());
      size_t globalWorkerIdOffset = 0;
      auto busyWait = std::chrono::microseconds(options.threadBusyWaitTime);
      for (size_t i = 0; i < numaNodes.size(); ++i) {
        std::string partitionName =
            options.poolName + " (NUMA " + std::to_string(i) + ")";
        CompactCPUDevicePtr numaDevicePtr = CompactCPUDevicePtr::reserve();
        std::unique_ptr<Allocator> partitionAllocator =
            getAllocator(options.getAllocatorOptions());
        std::unique_ptr<WorkQueue> partitionWorkQueue =
            createPartitionedThreadPoolWorkQueue(numaDevicePtr, numaNodes[i],
                                                 busyWait, partitionName,
                                                 globalWorkerIdOffset);
        globalWorkerIdOffset += partitionWorkQueue->getParallelismLevel();
        delegateWorkQueues.push_back(partitionWorkQueue.get());
        numaDevices[numaNodes[i]] =
            new CPUDevice(numaDevicePtr, std::move(partitionAllocator),
                          std::move(partitionWorkQueue), source,
                          CPUDeviceType::kNUMAPartition, numaNodes[i]);
      }
      workQueue = createDelegateThreadPoolWorkQueue(
          cpuDevicePtr, std::move(delegateWorkQueues));
      topLevelType = CPUDeviceType::kGlobalPartitioned;
    } else {
      workQueue = createThreadPoolWorkQueue(
          cpuDevicePtr, options.numThreads, options.maxThreads,
          options.mainWillDonate, options.withAffinity,
          std::chrono::microseconds(options.threadBusyWaitTime),
          options.poolName);
    }
    break;
  }
  CPUDeviceRef newCPUDevice = CPUDeviceRef::take(
      new CPUDevice(cpuDevicePtr, std::move(allocator), std::move(workQueue),
                    source, topLevelType, kAnyNumaNode, options.profileFilename,
                    options.runtimeProfilingTypeMask, options.profilerDebuginfo,
                    std::move(numaDevices)));

  getStoredGlobalCPUDeviceCreationOptions() = options;

  // Initialise the NUMA topology, to be used later when creating allocators and
  // work-queues.
  (void)NUMATopology::get();

  setGlobalCPUDevicePointer(newCPUDevice.getPointer());
  return newCPUDevice.copy();
}

using namespace M;
